## Breaking changes

### General

#### Nelm and werf binaries are built with Go 1.26 and require macOS 12 or later

<a id="distribution-os-requirements-go-1-26"></a>`distribution-os-requirements-go-1-26` · change · `distribution` `platform` · products: nelm, werf

Before: werf v2 release binaries were built with Go 1.23, which supports macOS 11 Big Sur and Linux kernel 2.6.32 or later. Nelm v1 release binaries were built with Go 1.24, which supports macOS 11 Big Sur and Linux kernel 3.2 or later.
Now: werf v3 and Nelm v2 are built with Go 1.26 (the `go` directive of their modules is `1.26`), so the macOS binaries require macOS 12 Monterey or later and the Linux binaries require kernel 3.2 or later (for Nelm the Linux requirement is unchanged). The set of published platforms is unchanged (`linux-amd64`, `linux-arm64`, `darwin-amd64`, `darwin-arm64`, `windows-amd64`).

**Migration:** Upgrade macOS hosts older than 12 Monterey before installing werf v3 or Nelm v2. werf only: upgrade Linux hosts with a kernel older than 3.2 before installing werf v3.

**References:** [werf@bc51d7214](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/bc51d7214f8e), [werf@dec66c577](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/dec66c577729), [nelm@d08c2937f](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/d08c2937f962), [nelm@fc44780e6](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/fc44780e6b4c), <https://go.dev/doc/go1.25#darwin>, <https://go.dev/doc/go1.24#linux>

#### The `preview-v2` feature gate is removed, its features are always on

<a id="feature-gate-preview-v2-removed"></a>`feature-gate-preview-v2-removed` · removal · `cli` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `NELM_FEAT_PREVIEW_V2=true` enabled at once the features planned for Nelm v2: `remote-charts`, `field-sensitive`, `clean-null-fields`, `more-detailed-exit-code-for-plan`, `native-release-list`, `native-release-uninstall` (and others). Each could also be enabled with its own `NELM_FEAT_*` variable.
Now: these behaviors are the default and their feature gates, including `preview-v2`, are removed. The `typescript` and `case-insensitive-condition-tracking` gates are removed too: TypeScript charts and case-insensitive condition matching are always on. Setting a removed `NELM_FEAT_*` variable prints an `Unsupported environment variable(s)` warning in the Nelm CLI; werf ignores it silently.

**Migration:** Remove `NELM_FEAT_PREVIEW_V2`, `NELM_FEAT_REMOTE_CHARTS`, `NELM_FEAT_FIELD_SENSITIVE`, `NELM_FEAT_CLEAN_NULL_FIELDS`, `NELM_FEAT_MORE_DETAILED_EXIT_CODE_FOR_PLAN`, `NELM_FEAT_RESOURCE_VALIDATION`, `NELM_FEAT_NATIVE_RELEASE_LIST`, `NELM_FEAT_NATIVE_RELEASE_UNINSTALL`, `NELM_FEAT_TYPESCRIPT` and `NELM_FEAT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_CONDITION_TRACKING` from the environment. If you did not use `preview-v2`, review the entries for each of these features: their behavior is now always on.

**References:** [nelm@07f2dfccd](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/07f2dfccdde2), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

### Deploy

#### Deploy and delete dependency annotations can wait for resources outside the release

<a id="dependency-annotations-external-auto"></a>`dependency-annotations-external-auto` · feature · `annotations` `plan` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `werf.io/deploy-dependency-<id>` and `werf.io/delete-dependency-<id>` could only point to resources of the release; a dependency that matched no release resource was ignored. Waiting for resources outside the release needed the separate `<id>.external-dependency.werf.io/*` annotations.
Now: both annotations accept `external=auto|true|false` (default `auto`).
- `external=true`, or `auto` when no release resource matches, makes the dependency external: Nelm waits for the resource in the cluster to be `present`/`ready` (deploy) or `absent` (delete). `kind`, `version` and `name` must then be specified, plus `group` for non-core groups and `namespace` if it is not the release namespace.
- `external=false` restricts the dependency to release resources.
- With `external` omitted, a dependency missing `name`, `kind` or `version` is treated as internal, so incomplete annotations, including those stored in older releases, keep working; Nelm warns once when such an internal dependency matches no release resource.
External dependencies are not forced into readiness tracking of release resources.

**Migration:** Check `werf.io/deploy-dependency-*` and `werf.io/delete-dependency-*` annotations that fully specify `kind`, `version` and `name` of a resource that is not in the release: they used to be ignored and now make the deploy or deletion wait for that resource in the cluster. Add `external=false` to keep ignoring it, or remove the annotation.

**References:** [werf#8081](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8081), [werf#8114](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8114), [nelm#617](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/617), [nelm@b4771c646](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/b4771c646ede), [nelm#755](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/755), [nelm#769](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/769)

#### Deploy, rollback and uninstall reports identify their format with `"apiVersion": "v3"`

<a id="deploy-report-api-version"></a>`deploy-report-api-version` · change · `deploy-report` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the JSON reports saved with `--save-report-to` (Nelm) or `--save-deploy-report`, `--save-rollback-report`, `--save-uninstall-report` (werf) had a numeric `"version": 3` field.
Now: the field is replaced with the string `"apiVersion": "v3"`; `version` is no longer written. In the Go API, `ReleaseReportV3.Version int` is replaced with `ReleaseReportV3.APIVersion string`.

**Migration:** Update scripts that read or validate `version` to check `apiVersion == "v3"` instead.

**References:** [nelm#607](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/607)

#### Diffs of Secrets and resources marked `werf.io/sensitive` hide only `data` and `stringData` values

<a id="deploy-sensitive-data-and-stringdata-only"></a>`deploy-sensitive-data-and-stringdata-only` · change · `plan` `annotations` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the whole diff of a `v1/Secret` and of any resource annotated `werf.io/sensitive: "true"` was replaced with `<hidden sensitive changes>`. The selective behavior was opt-in through the `field-sensitive` or `preview-v2` feature gates (`NELM_FEAT_FIELD_SENSITIVE=true`, `NELM_FEAT_PREVIEW_V2=true`).
Now: for such resources only values at `data.*` and `stringData.*` are hidden (replaced with length and hash information); metadata, key names and all other fields are shown in the diff. `werf.io/sensitive-paths` still overrides the default path list. The feature gate is removed.

**Migration:** If a resource keeps sensitive data outside `data`/`stringData` (e.g. in `spec`), annotate it with `werf.io/sensitive-paths` listing the JSONPath expressions to hide, e.g. `"$.spec.token"`; include `$.data.*` and `$.stringData.*` too if needed, since the annotation replaces the default list. Remove `NELM_FEAT_FIELD_SENSITIVE` from the environment.

**References:** [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### Encrypted secret values keep their YAML type, style and comments

<a id="secrets-yaml-value-types-preserved"></a>`secrets-yaml-value-types-preserved` · change · `secrets` `values` · products: nelm, werf

Before: encrypting a value in a secret values file stored only its text, so every encrypted value was decrypted as a string: `port: 8080` became `port: "8080"`, `enabled: true` became `"true"`. Block scalar style and comments on encrypted values were dropped.
Now: newly encrypted values store their YAML tag and scalar style, so numbers, booleans and other types stay typed after decryption and block scalars keep their style. Changing only the type of a value (e.g. `"8080"` to `8080`) now re-encrypts it. Comments attached to encrypted values are preserved and stay in cleartext in the encrypted file, like keys.
Values encrypted before this change never stored their type: they are still read as strings, and decrypting and encrypting the file again does not restore the type.

**Migration:** Values you newly enter as unquoted numbers or booleans are now passed to templates and `values.schema.json` as numbers or booleans, not strings: quote them if templates expect strings. To give an old value its type, re-enter it with `werf helm secret values edit` / `nelm chart secret values-file edit`. Do not put secrets in comments of secret values files.

**References:** [common-go#37](https://github.com/werf/common-go/pull/37)

#### Helm path environment variables `HELM_CACHE_HOME`, `HELM_CONFIG_HOME`, `HELM_DATA_HOME` and `HELM_REPOSITORY_*` are no longer read

<a id="charts-helm-path-env-vars-ignored"></a>`charts-helm-path-env-vars-ignored` · removal · `charts` `dependencies` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the Helm cache, config and data directories could be moved with `HELM_CACHE_HOME`, `HELM_CONFIG_HOME` and `HELM_DATA_HOME`, and chart download and dependency resolution during render, lint, plan and install also honored `HELM_REPOSITORY_CONFIG`, `HELM_REPOSITORY_CACHE` and `HELM_CONTENT_CACHE`.
Now: `HELM_CACHE_HOME`, `HELM_CONFIG_HOME` and `HELM_DATA_HOME` are ignored everywhere, and render, lint, plan and install commands also ignore `HELM_REPOSITORY_CONFIG`, `HELM_REPOSITORY_CACHE` and `HELM_CONTENT_CACHE` (the Helm-based `nelm chart repo` commands still read them). The chart repository list and the chart caches are located only via `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME`, by default `~/.config/helm`, `~/.cache/helm` and `~/.local/share/helm` on Linux. The XDG variables point to the parent directory: with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/custom/config`, `/custom/config/helm/repositories.yaml` is read.

**Migration:** If you set `HELM_CONFIG_HOME`/`HELM_REPOSITORY_CONFIG` or the cache variables, copy `repositories.yaml` to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/helm/repositories.yaml` (or `~/.config/helm/`) or add the repositories again, and set `XDG_CACHE_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` instead of the `HELM_*` variables.

**References:** [werf#7518](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7518), [nelm#611](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/611)

#### Installing from a saved plan respects `--release-history-limit`

<a id="plan-use-plan-release-history-limit"></a>`plan-use-plan-release-history-limit` · fix · `plan` `release-storage` `go-api` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm release install --use-plan` (werf: `werf converge --use-plan`) took the release history limit from the saved plan, where it was always `0`, so old release revisions were never pruned and the history grew without limit.
Now: the history limit comes from `--release-history-limit` of the install command (default `10`), as without `--use-plan`.
Go API: `ReleaseHistoryLimit` moved from `common.ReleaseInstallRuntimeOptions` to `action.ReleaseInstallOptions` (as in `ReleaseRollbackOptions` and `ReleaseUninstallOptions`) and is no longer stored in plan artifacts.
In werf, `werf converge --use-plan` and `werf bundle apply --use-plan` now respect `--releases-history-max` (`$WERF_RELEASES_HISTORY_MAX`).

**Migration:** Go API callers that set `ReleaseHistoryLimit` inside a `common.ReleaseInstallRuntimeOptions` literal must set `action.ReleaseInstallOptions.ReleaseHistoryLimit` instead. Releases installed from saved plans may have accumulated many revisions; the next install prunes them down to the limit.

**References:** [werf#8085](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8085), [nelm@65c01393d](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/65c01393de40)

#### Lookalike keys such as `werf-io/weight` no longer act as `werf.io/*` and `helm.sh/*` annotations

<a id="annotations-lookalike-keys-ignored"></a>`annotations-lookalike-keys-ignored` · fix · `annotations` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the patterns for Nelm's annotation and label keys didn't escape the dot, so any character in place of a `.` matched: `werf-io/weight`, `helm-sh/hook`, `werfXio/deploy-dependency-foo` etc. were validated and applied as `werf.io/weight`, `helm.sh/hook` and so on (e.g. `werf-io/weight: "abc"` failed the deploy with `invalid value "abc" for annotation "werf-io/weight"`).
Now: only the exactly spelled `werf.io/*`, `helm.sh/*`, `meta.helm.sh/*` and `app.kubernetes.io/*` keys are recognized; lookalike keys are ignored by Nelm.

**Migration:** If a chart relied on a misspelled key such as `werf-io/weight` or `helm-sh/hook`, rename it to the dotted key (`werf.io/weight`, `helm.sh/hook`).

**References:** [werf#8132](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8132), [nelm#799](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/799)

#### Non-string annotation and label values fail rendering instead of being dropped

<a id="render-invalid-annotations-labels-fail"></a>`render-invalid-annotations-labels-fail` · change · `render` `validation` `annotations` · products: nelm, werf

Before: entries of `metadata.annotations` and `metadata.labels` in chart manifests whose value was not a string (e.g. an unquoted number or boolean) were dropped with a warning, and the resource was deployed without them.
Now: such a value fails rendering, linting, planning and installing with a `decode resource (file: "..."): ...` error. Resources already stored in a release are not rejected: their invalid entries are dropped with a warning. Go API users can restore the old behavior with the new `DropInvalidAnnotationsAndLabels` option of `ChartRenderOptions`, `ChartLintOptions`, `ReleaseInstallOptions` and `ReleasePlanInstallOptions`.

**Migration:** Quote numbers and booleans in annotations and labels in templates, e.g. `example.com/replicas: "3"` or `{{ .Values.x | quote }}`.

**References:** [nelm#614](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/614)

#### Null fields are removed from rendered manifests by default

<a id="deploy-null-fields-cleaned-by-default"></a>`deploy-null-fields-cleaned-by-default` · change · `render` `resources` · products: nelm, werf

Before: fields and list entries with a `null` value were kept in rendered manifests and sent to the cluster as is. Removing them was opt-in through the `clean-null-fields` or `preview-v2` feature gates (`NELM_FEAT_CLEAN_NULL_FIELDS=true`, `NELM_FEAT_PREVIEW_V2=true`).
Now: `null` fields and list entries are removed recursively from all rendered resources, as Helm does, both for deploy and for the manifests printed by `render` commands. The feature gate is removed and there is no switch to restore the previous behavior.

**Migration:** Check resources that intentionally set a field to `null` (an absent field and an explicit `null` are not always equivalent for Kubernetes and CRDs) and set an explicit value instead. Remove `NELM_FEAT_CLEAN_NULL_FIELDS` from the environment.

**References:** [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc), [nelm@e9bbd6e25](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/e9bbd6e25a02)

#### OCI charts are pulled by one manifest digest with stricter provenance verification

<a id="charts-oci-pull-digest-pinned"></a>`charts-oci-pull-digest-pinned` · change · `charts` `oci` `registry` · products: nelm, werf

Changes for remote `oci://` charts in `release install`, `release plan install`, `chart render`, `chart lint` and `chart download`:
- A tag is resolved to a manifest digest once, and the chart and its provenance are fetched by that digest (the provenance never comes from a cache). The resolved digest is logged (`Resolved chart … to digest …`, and `Verified chart … signed by …` after verification).
- With `--provenance-strategy` `verify` or `verify-if-possible`, a semver tag (leading `v` dropped, `_` read as `+`) must equal the chart version; `verify` without `--provenance-keyring` fails before downloading, and a signed chart under `verify-if-possible` without a keyring fails. A tag ending in `.prov` is rejected.
- An OCI chart can be pulled by an existing non-semver tag (e.g. `oci://repo/chart:latest`).
- Install, plan, render and lint download charts into a private per-invocation directory that is removed afterwards, not into Helm's shared repository cache.
- Nelm: in install, plan, render and lint, `--chart-repo-ca`, `--chart-repo-cert`/`--chart-repo-key`, `--no-verify-chart-repos-tls` and `--chart-repo-request-timeout` now apply to `oci://` charts; basic-auth credentials are sent only to the chart's host. `nelm chart download` keeps Helm's flags (`--ca-file`, `--cert-file`, `--key-file`, `--insecure-skip-tls-verify`, `--plain-http`). Loopback registries (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`) are reached over plain HTTP unless TLS options are given; with `--insecure-chart-repos` plain HTTP is always used.
- werf: bundles are pulled with `--insecure-registry` (plain HTTP) and `--skip-tls-verify-registry`; dependency charts use `--skip-tls-verify-helm-dependencies`. werf has no option for a custom CA file.

**Migration:** If you verify provenance of OCI charts, make sure the tag you deploy equals the chart version (or deploy by digest) and pass `--provenance-keyring`. For OCI registries with self-signed certificates, pass the CA with `--chart-repo-ca` in Nelm (`--ca-file` for `nelm chart download`); in werf, add the CA to the system trust store, or as a last resort use `--skip-tls-verify-registry` (bundles) or `--skip-tls-verify-helm-dependencies` (dependencies).

**References:** [werf#8144](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8144), [nelm#811](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/811)

#### Offline rendering assumes Kubernetes 1.36.0 by default

<a id="render-default-kube-version-1-36"></a>`render-default-kube-version-1-36` · change · `render` · products: nelm, werf

Before: without cluster access (`nelm chart render`, `nelm chart lint`, `werf render`, `werf lint`, `werf bundle render`), `.Capabilities.KubeVersion` defaulted to `1.20.0`.
Now: the default is `1.36.0`. Templates that branch on `.Capabilities.KubeVersion` (e.g. choose API versions) may render differently.

**Migration:** Pass `--kube-version 1.20.0` to keep the previous rendering, or update the templates.

**References:** [nelm@2159f9621](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/2159f962147e)

#### Packed charts keep their publish-time inputs in `.werf-data/` and are deployed as if those inputs were passed again

<a id="charts-werf-data-publish-inputs"></a>`charts-werf-data-publish-inputs` · change · `charts` `values` `bundles` · products: nelm, werf

New: `nelm chart pack` (and `werf bundle publish`, which uses the same code) stores the inputs given at pack time in a `.werf-data/` directory at the chart root, next to the unchanged chart files: `metadata.yaml` (`--set*` options, `--set-root-json`, patches, disable switches such as `--no-default-values`, annotations and labels, release name and namespace), `values.yaml` (merged `--values` files), `secret-values.yaml` (merged `--secret-values` files, still encrypted), `extra-values.yaml` (service values, e.g. werf's) and `set-files/` (`--set-file` contents). Helm, Argo CD and Flux ignore the directory and install the chart with its own values.
Install, plan, render and lint of such a chart replay these inputs as values layers, so the result and the stored release values are the same as deploying the source chart with the pack-time flags: chart values < chart secret values < pack-time `--values` < `--secret-values` < `--set*` < extra values < deploy-time `--values` < `--secret-values` < `--set*` < service values. Deploy-time `--set*` patch the result of pack-time `--set*`. Pack-time patches are applied between the chart's `patches.yaml` and `--patches`; pack-time annotations and labels are merged below the deploy-time ones. A dependency with its own `.werf-data/` renders like that chart deployed alone, under the parent's values. One info line lists what was loaded from `.werf-data/`.
An empty release name or namespace of `release install`, `release plan install`, `chart render` and `chart lint` is taken from the release recorded in `.werf-data/metadata.yaml`; `--release`/`--namespace` of `release install` and `release plan install` are therefore optional and fail with `release name and release namespace required: not given and not recorded in the chart's .werf-data` only when neither is available. Charts packed by an older format (legacy werf bundles) get the annotations and labels of their `extra_annotations.json`/`extra_labels.json`.
A chart whose `.werf-data/metadata.yaml` has an unknown `apiVersion` fails with `this chart requires a newer Nelm version`.
Old clients: werf v2.85.0 and newer v2 releases refuse such a chart with `it requires werf v3 or Nelm v2, or newer` (werf/werf#8141). Nelm v1.31.3, werf v2.84.1 and earlier, and werf v3.0–v3.12 do not know `.werf-data/` and deploy it without its publish-time inputs (no image values, publish-time values, secrets or annotations), without an error; the same check for Nelm v1 (werf/nelm#808) is not released yet.
werf bundles:
Before: `werf bundle publish` merged the image values, the publish-time `--values`, `--set*` and service values into `values.yaml` of the published chart and the chart and `--secret-values` secret values into its `secret-values.yaml`, and saved annotations and labels in `extra_annotations.json`/`extra_labels.json`. Because the inputs were flattened, a published bundle could render differently from `werf converge` with the same flags (export/import-values, `--set` patching, nulls, `--set-json` replacements, disabled default secrets).
Now: the chart is published unchanged (`Chart.yaml` keeps comments and order; only `name`, `version` and the `helm.sh/images` annotation with the built images and digests are set, and a missing `apiVersion` becomes `v2`). Everything werf adds is stored in `.werf-data/` of the chart: `--values`, `--secret-values` (still encrypted), `--set*`, `--set-file` contents, `--set-root-json`, `--patches`, the disable switches, the image/repo/env/commit service values, annotations and labels, and the release name and namespace. `werf bundle apply`, `werf bundle plan` and `werf bundle render` replay them as values layers, so the result and the stored release values match `werf converge`; `.Chart.Name` and `.Chart.Version` (repository basename, version from the tag) are the known difference.
- Helm, Argo CD and Flux installing a published bundle get only the chart's own `values.yaml`: no image values, publish-time values, secrets or annotations.
- werf v2 cannot deploy the new bundles: werf v2.85.0 and newer v2 releases refuse them, werf v2.84.1 and earlier and werf v3.0–v3.12 deploy them without images and publish-time values; the new format needs werf v3.13+. Bundles published by werf v2 are still deployed by werf v3 unchanged, except that for them the annotations passed to `werf bundle apply`/`plan`/`render` (`--add-annotation`, werf service annotations such as `project.werf.io/env`) now win per key over the bundle's `extra_annotations.json`; before, the bundle's `project.werf.io/*`, `ci.werf.io/*` and `werf.io/release-channel` won.
- Publish-time `--secret-values` are saved decrypted in the release at apply, like `werf converge --secret-values`, so `werf release get --print-values` shows them; the first apply of a new bundle over an old release creates a new revision.
- `--disable-default-values` and `--disable-default-secret-values` of `werf bundle apply` ignore only the chart's own files, not the values stored at publish. Disable switches recorded in a committed `.werf-data/metadata.yaml` (e.g. an unpacked published chart committed as `.helm`) are kept by `werf bundle publish` and can only be cleared by editing that file.
- New `werf bundle publish` options: `--patches` and `--no-default-patches`.
- `--tag` of `werf bundle publish`: a strict semver tag (a leading `v` dropped) is the chart version, anything else gives `0.0.0-<unix time>-<tag slug>` (at most 128 characters); the chart is pushed under the version tag and, if different, under the literal tag (`+` pushed as `_`). Publish refuses a tag that equals a werf image tag in the same repository.
- Without `--release`/`--namespace`, `werf bundle apply`/`plan`/`render` use the ones recorded at publish, unless a non-empty `--env` differs from the publish-time env; then both flags are required.
- `--provenance-strategy=verify`/`verify-if-possible` verify bundles pulled from a registry; `verify` with `--bundle-dir` fails.
- `werf converge`, `werf render`, `werf plan` and `werf lint` honor a committed `.helm/.werf-data/`; `.werf-data/` is never excluded by `.helmignore`. A werf-published chart used as a dependency gets its publish-time values folded into its defaults; its annotations, labels, patches and release defaults are ignored with a warning.
Go API: `action.ChartPack`, `action.ResolveRecordedRelease`, `chart.DownloadChart`, `*action.ReleaseRequiredError`; the loaded chart gets `WerfDataFiles`.

**Migration:** Upgrade every Nelm and werf that installs, plans, renders or lints published charts or bundles (Nelm v2, werf v3) before publishing with `nelm chart pack` or werf v3 `werf bundle publish`: do not rely on old clients failing. Rename an unrelated existing `.werf-data/` directory at the chart root: it is now interpreted as publish-time inputs and never excluded by `.helmignore`.
werf: When installing published bundles with Helm, Argo CD or Flux, pass `.werf-data/values.yaml` and `.werf-data/extra-values.yaml` as values files (publish-time `--set*` and secrets stay unavailable to them). Pass `--release`/`--namespace` when applying a bundle with a different `--env` than at publish. Expect one new revision on the first apply of a bundle that uses `--secret-values`.

**References:** [werf#8142](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8142), [werf#8144](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8144), [werf#8159](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8159), [nelm#809](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/809), [nelm#811](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/811), [nelm#823](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/823), <https://werf.io/docs/v3/resources/migration_from_v2_to_v3.html#charts-and-bundles>

#### Plan with `--exit-code` returns 3 when only the release needs to be installed

<a id="plan-detailed-exit-code"></a>`plan-detailed-exit-code` · change · `plan` `cli` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm release plan install --exit-code`, `werf plan --exit-code` and `werf bundle plan --exit-code` returned `2` for any planned change, including a release-only update with no resource changes. The extended codes were opt-in through the `more-detailed-exit-code-for-plan` or `preview-v2` feature gates.
Now: exit codes are `0` — no changes, `1` — error, `2` — resource changes planned, `3` — no resource changes, but the release still has to be installed. The feature gate is removed.

**Migration:** Update CI that only accepts `0` and `2` to also handle `3` (not an error, but the release still needs installing). Remove `NELM_FEAT_MORE_DETAILED_EXIT_CODE_FOR_PLAN` from the environment.

**References:** [werf@0b50bd1bb](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/0b50bd1bbf42), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### Readiness tracking matches status condition types of custom resources case-insensitively

<a id="tracking-condition-types-case-insensitive"></a>`tracking-condition-types-case-insensitive` · change · `tracking` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the built-in readiness rules for custom resources only matched lowercase condition types in `status.conditions` (`ready`, `available`, ...). A resource with a CamelCase condition such as `Ready` or `Available` matched no rule and was reported ready as soon as it appeared. Case-insensitive matching was available only as an opt-in through the `case-insensitive-condition-tracking` feature gate (`NELM_FEAT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_CONDITION_TRACKING=true`).
Now: condition types are always matched case-insensitively, CamelCase first. A custom resource with a `Ready`/`Available` condition is reported ready only once that condition is `True`, so deploys wait for it and may time out if it never becomes `True`. The feature gate is removed; `NELM_FEAT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_CONDITION_TRACKING` is reported as an unsupported environment variable.

**Migration:** Check custom resources that have `Ready` or `Available` conditions: the deploy now waits for them. If a resource never reaches `True` and should not block the deploy, set `werf.io/track-termination-mode: NonBlocking` on it, or fix its controller. Remove `NELM_FEAT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_CONDITION_TRACKING` from the environment.

**References:** [werf#7805](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7805), [nelm@0585a1f40](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/0585a1f4041e), [nelm@ca3aa25c8](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/ca3aa25c8f4f), [kubedog@e8f61a4bc](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/commit/e8f61a4bc90a), [kubedog@438ef109f](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/commit/438ef109f804)

#### Render and diff patches modify rendered resources and drift detection with jq

<a id="resource-patches"></a>`resource-patches` · feature · `patches` `render` · products: nelm, werf

New: rendered resources can be patched with jq programs, from `patches.yaml` in the root of the chart and its subcharts (read automatically) and from files passed with `--patches`. Two kinds of patches:
- `renderPatches` modify resources after rendering and before deploy, like Helm's `--post-renderer`, e.g. to change what a third-party subchart doesn't let you configure. A render patch can't change `apiVersion`, `kind`, `name` or `namespace`, and can read `$Values`, `$Release`, `$Chart` and `$Capabilities` — the same data the templates of the chart that ships `patches.yaml` see (the top-level chart for `--patches` files).
- `diffPatches` don't change what is deployed: they are applied to both the live and the to-be version of a resource when deciding whether to update it, so changes in the patched fields are ignored.
Each rule has a `match` (kinds, groups, versions, names, namespaces, labels, annotations, `charts`; `/.../` values are regular expressions) and a `patch`. `patches.yaml` applies only to resources of its chart and subcharts; `--patches` files apply to all resources. Patches are applied in order, each to the result of the previous one: subcharts, then the parent chart, then `--patches` files. `release rollback` and `release uninstall` apply only diff patches. jq `debug` and `debug(msg)` print to the log at `--log-level debug` or `trace`, naming the patch rule and resource.
`--no-default-patches` ignores `patches.yaml` of all charts.
Go API: `LegacyPatches` (`spec.Patches`) on render, lint, install, plan install, rollback and uninstall options passes rules programmatically, applied after `PatchesFiles`.
In werf, `werf converge`, `werf plan`, `werf render`, `werf lint`, `werf rollback`, `werf dismiss`, `werf bundle apply`, `werf bundle plan` and `werf bundle render` accept `--patches` (`$WERF_PATCHES`, `$WERF_PATCHES_*`) and `--no-default-patches` (`$WERF_NO_DEFAULT_PATCHES`).

**Migration:** A `patches.yaml` file in the root of a chart or subchart is now read automatically. If your chart has a file with this name that serves another purpose, rename it or pass `--no-default-patches` (`WERF_NO_DEFAULT_PATCHES=true` in werf); otherwise it may change manifests or fail the deploy.

**References:** [werf#7661](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7661), [werf#7735](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7735), [werf#7815](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7815), [werf#7958](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7958), [nelm@9241ea8a5](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/9241ea8a51d0), [nelm#696](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/696), [nelm#720](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/720), [nelm#727](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/727), [nelm#785](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/785)

#### Rendered manifests are ordered CRDs first, then all other resources by kind and name

<a id="render-resource-output-order"></a>`render-resource-output-order` · change · `render` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm chart render`, `werf render` and `werf bundle render` printed standalone CRDs (from `crds/`) first, then all `helm.sh/hook` resources, then the regular resources, each group sorted by kind, group, version, namespace and name.
Now: all CRDs (from `crds/`, templates or hooks) come first, then all other resources, hooks and regular resources together, sorted by kind, group, version, namespace and name. The set of rendered resources and their content are unchanged.

**Migration:** If a script relies on the position of hooks in the render output (e.g. compares it with a saved copy), regenerate the saved copy or select resources by their annotations instead of their position.

**References:** [nelm@55bc4628d](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/55bc4628d79e)

#### Resource validation uses Kubernetes and CRD schemas embedded into the binary

<a id="resource-validation-embedded-schemas"></a>`resource-validation-embedded-schemas` · change · `validation` · products: nelm, werf

Before: resource validation downloaded JSON schemas from the network (`--resource-validation-schema`, by default the `yannh/kubernetes-json-schema` and `datreeio/CRDs-catalog` repositories) for one Kubernetes version (`--resource-validation-kube-version`, default `1.35.0`); `--local-resource-validation` disabled the network sources.
Now: the Kubernetes schemas of the last five Kubernetes minor versions (merged, newest wins) and the `datreeio/CRDs-catalog` CRD schemas are embedded into the binary, so validation works offline. A resource kind without a schema is skipped. `--resource-validation-extra-schema` adds schema sources that take precedence over the embedded ones. The `--resource-validation-schema`, `--resource-validation-kube-version` and `--local-resource-validation` flags are removed. The embedded schemas are refreshed with new releases.

**Migration:** Remove `--resource-validation-schema`, `--resource-validation-kube-version` and `--local-resource-validation` (and their environment variables) from your scripts. To validate against your own schemas, pass them with `--resource-validation-extra-schema`.

**References:** [werf#7729](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7729), [werf#7760](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7760), [nelm#673](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/673), [nelm@9d049189c](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/9d049189ce4e), [nelm#778](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/778)

#### Resources are deleted with Background propagation by default

<a id="deploy-delete-propagation-background"></a>`deploy-delete-propagation-background` · change · `resources` `uninstall` · products: nelm, werf

Before: resources were deleted with `Foreground` propagation: deletion of a resource (e.g. a Deployment) finished only after its dependents (ReplicaSets, Pods) were gone.
Now: the default is `Background`: the resource is deleted immediately and its dependents are garbage-collected afterwards, so subsequent steps no longer wait for them. This applies to deletion during install, rollback and uninstall, and to recreation of resources.

**Migration:** If a later step depends on dependents being gone, set the `werf.io/delete-propagation: Foreground` annotation on the resource, or pass `--delete-propagation=Foreground` (`NELM_DELETE_PROPAGATION` / `WERF_DELETE_PROPAGATION`).

**References:** [nelm#623](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/623)

#### Resources are validated against Kubernetes JSON schemas by default

<a id="resource-validation-enabled-by-default"></a>`resource-validation-enabled-by-default` · change · `validation` `resources` · products: nelm, werf

Before: validating rendered resources against Kubernetes JSON schemas, and the `--no-resource-validation`, `--resource-validation-*` flags, were available only with the `resource-validation` feature gate (`NELM_FEAT_RESOURCE_VALIDATION=true`).
Now: resource validation is on by default in `nelm release install`, `nelm release plan install`, `nelm release rollback` and `nelm chart lint`, and in `werf converge`, `werf plan`, `werf rollback`, `werf lint`, `werf bundle apply` and `werf bundle plan`; manifests that do not match the schema of their kind are rejected before being applied. The `--no-resource-validation`, `--resource-validation-skip`, `--resource-validation-extra-schema` and `--resource-validation-cache-lifetime` flags are always available. The feature gate is removed. Render commands (`nelm chart render`, `werf render`, `werf bundle render`) do not run this validation: use lint to check resources against the schemas.

**Migration:** Fix resources that fail validation. Skip specific resources with `--resource-validation-skip` (e.g. `kind=MyKind`), add schemas for custom resources with `--resource-validation-extra-schema`, or disable validation entirely with `--no-resource-validation`. Remove `NELM_FEAT_RESOURCE_VALIDATION` from the environment.

**References:** [werf@0b50bd1bb](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/0b50bd1bbf42), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### Runtime annotations and labels appear in rendered manifests and changes to them alone do not update resources

<a id="render-runtime-annotations-and-labels"></a>`render-runtime-annotations-and-labels` · change · `render` `annotations` `plan` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm chart render` and `werf render`/`werf bundle render` ignored runtime annotations: `--runtime-annotations` of Nelm and werf's service annotations (`werf.io/version`, `project.werf.io/name`, `project.werf.io/env`, `ci.werf.io/*`, `werf.io/release-channel`) were not in the output. During install, plan and rollback, only werf's own service annotations were ignored when deciding whether a resource needs an update; a change in the value of a custom `--runtime-annotations`/`--runtime-labels` entry alone triggered an update.
Now: runtime annotations and labels (`--runtime-annotations`, `--runtime-labels` in Nelm; the service annotations in werf) are added to the rendered manifests. Install, plan and rollback ignore all runtime annotations and labels when deciding whether a live resource differs from the chart, so changing only their values does not update resources; they are applied together with other changes.

**Migration:** If you compare render output with saved manifests or feed it to other tools, expect the additional runtime annotations and labels (in werf: `werf.io/version`, `project.werf.io/name`, `project.werf.io/env` and others). Use regular `--annotations`/`--labels` (werf: `--add-annotation`/`--add-label`) for metadata whose change must update resources.

**References:** [nelm#615](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/615)

#### SQL release storage keeps release annotations in a new `nelm_release_annotations_v1` table

<a id="release-storage-sql-annotations-table"></a>`release-storage-sql-annotations-table` · change · `release-storage` · products: nelm, werf

Before: SQL (PostgreSQL) release storage used only Helm's `releases_v1` table and the `gorp_migrations` table.
Now: on first use Nelm runs an extra migration, recorded in a new `nelm_migrations` table, which creates the `nelm_release_annotations_v1` table (release annotations, referencing `releases_v1` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`), grants `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on it and `SELECT` on `nelm_migrations` to `PUBLIC`, and enables row-level security on it. Release annotations are written there in the same transaction as the release and read from it without loading release bodies; the annotations are still kept in the release body for Helm compatibility. If the table can't be read, annotations are read from the body. A write denied by permissions fails with `access to table "nelm_release_annotations_v1" for release namespace "<ns>": check the current role's table privileges and row-level security (RLS) policies`.

**Migration:** If Nelm/werf connects to PostgreSQL with a role that can't create tables, run the first deploy of the new version with a role that can (or apply the migration as a database administrator), so that `nelm_migrations` and `nelm_release_annotations_v1` are created. Row-level security is enabled on `nelm_release_annotations_v1` without policies, so a role that doesn't own the table can't access its rows: create RLS policies for the roles that deploy releases, e.g. per release namespace, matching the policies you use for `releases_v1`.

**References:** [werf#8084](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8084), [nelm#752](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/752)

#### Saved plan artifacts use format `v2`, plans saved by the previous version are rejected

<a id="plan-artifact-format-v2"></a>`plan-artifact-format-v2` · change · `plan` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the plan file written by `nelm release plan install --save-plan` (werf: `werf plan --save-plan`) had `apiVersion: v1` and stored the release in the Helm 3 release format; the version was not checked on `--use-plan`.
Now: the plan file has `apiVersion: v2` and stores the release in a format that also covers `apiVersion: v3` charts. `nelm release install --use-plan`, `nelm release plan show` and `werf converge --use-plan` reject a plan file of another version with `plan artifact <version> is not supported by the current version`.

**Migration:** Do not carry plan files across the upgrade: re-run `plan --save-plan` with the new version before applying.

**References:** [nelm@ae98e045c](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/ae98e045c538)

#### Secrets are encrypted with authenticated AES-GCM that older versions cannot decrypt

<a id="secrets-authenticated-encryption-format"></a>`secrets-authenticated-encryption-format` · change · `secrets` · products: nelm, werf

Before: secret values files (`secret-values.yaml`) and secret files were encrypted with AES-CBC without an integrity check: a corrupted or modified ciphertext could decrypt to garbage, and a wrong secret key was often accepted.
Now: everything that is written (`werf helm secret values edit`/`encrypt`, `werf helm secret file edit`/`encrypt`, `nelm chart secret values-file edit`/`encrypt`, `nelm chart secret file edit`/`encrypt`, and release plans saved with a secret key) uses authenticated AES-GCM: format version 2 for whole files, version 3 for individual YAML values. Tampering and wrong keys are reported as errors. Values encrypted in the old AES-CBC format are still decrypted as before, and the secret key format is unchanged. There is no option to write the old format.
Older werf and Nelm versions cannot decrypt the new format and fail, e.g. with a `decode file ...` error. When only some values of a file are edited, only those values are re-encrypted; the others keep the old format.

**Migration:** Before the first `edit` or `encrypt` with werf v3 / Nelm v2, upgrade every environment that reads the repository's secrets: developer machines, CI jobs, and jobs that apply saved release plans. After secrets are re-encrypted, an old werf or Nelm must not handle the repository; switching back does not restore the old format.

**References:** [werf#7818](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7818), [nelm#706](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/706), [common-go#37](https://github.com/werf/common-go/pull/37)

#### The `--set-runtime-json` option and `$.Runtime` are removed

<a id="values-set-runtime-json-removed"></a>`values-set-runtime-json-removed` · removal · `values` `cli` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `--set-runtime-json` (`$NELM_SET_RUNTIME_JSON`, werf: `$WERF_SET_RUNTIME_JSON`) set keys under `$.Runtime`, available in chart templates.
Now: the option is removed and `$.Runtime` is no longer populated in templates.

**Migration:** Pass the data as values with `--set-json` and read it from `.Values` in templates. Remove `--set-runtime-json` from scripts: an unknown flag fails argument parsing.

**References:** [werf@0b50bd1bb](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/0b50bd1bbf42), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### The `--show-verbose-diffs` option is removed, diffs of created and deleted resources are always shown

<a id="plan-show-verbose-diffs-removed"></a>`plan-show-verbose-diffs-removed` · removal · `plan` `cli` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm release plan install`, `nelm release plan show`, `werf plan` and `werf bundle plan` had `--show-verbose-diffs` (default `true`); with `false`, diffs of created and deleted resources were replaced with `<hidden verbose changes>`.
Now: the option is removed and full diffs of created and deleted resources are always shown.

**Migration:** Remove `--show-verbose-diffs` and `WERF_SHOW_VERBOSE_DIFFS`/`NELM_*_SHOW_VERBOSE_DIFFS` from scripts: an unknown flag fails argument parsing.

**References:** [werf@0b50bd1bb](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/0b50bd1bbf42), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### The `<id>.external-dependency.werf.io/resource` and `/namespace` annotations are removed

<a id="annotations-external-dependency-removed"></a>`annotations-external-dependency-removed` · removal · `annotations` `tracking` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `<id>.external-dependency.werf.io/resource: <kind>[.<version>.<group>]/<name>` together with `<id>.external-dependency.werf.io/namespace` made a resource wait until a resource outside the release was present and ready. The undocumented `<id>.external-dependency.werf.io: <apiVersion>:<kind>[:<namespace>]:<name>` form worked too.
Now: these annotations are not supported: a warning `annotation "..." in resource "..." is no longer supported, use "werf.io/deploy-dependency-<id>" or "werf.io/delete-dependency-<id>" instead` is printed and the resource does not wait for the external resource.

**Migration:** Replace them with `werf.io/deploy-dependency-<id>`, specifying `kind`, `version`, `name`, `group` for a resource of a non-core group, and `namespace` if it differs from the release namespace, e.g. `secret.external-dependency.werf.io/resource: secret/my-vault-secret` + `secret.external-dependency.werf.io/namespace: vault` become `werf.io/deploy-dependency-secret: state=ready,kind=Secret,version=v1,name=my-vault-secret,namespace=vault,external=true`.

**References:** [nelm#625](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/625)

#### The deprecated `<name>.dependency.werf.io` annotation is removed

<a id="annotations-legacy-dependency-werf-io-removed"></a>`annotations-legacy-dependency-werf-io-removed` · removal · `annotations` · products: nelm, werf

Before: an undocumented, deprecated `<name>.dependency.werf.io: <apiVersion>:<kind>[:<namespace>]:<name>` annotation made the resource wait until the given release resource was present.
Now: the annotation is ignored without a warning.

**Migration:** Replace it with `werf.io/deploy-dependency-<name>: state=present,kind=<kind>,version=<version>[,group=<group>],name=<name>[,namespace=<namespace>]`.

**References:** [nelm@be2f6f8e2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/be2f6f8e20d6)

#### The duplicate `--save-rollback-graph-to` option is removed from `release install` and `release rollback`

<a id="cli-save-rollback-graph-to-removed"></a>`cli-save-rollback-graph-to-removed` · removal · `cli` `rollback` · products: nelm

Before: `nelm release install` and `nelm release rollback` accepted `--save-rollback-graph-to` (`$NELM_RELEASE_INSTALL_SAVE_ROLLBACK_GRAPH_TO`, `$NELM_RELEASE_ROLLBACK_SAVE_ROLLBACK_GRAPH_TO`). In `release rollback` it duplicated `--save-graph-to`.
Now: the option is removed from both commands. `nelm release rollback` keeps `--save-graph-to`; `nelm release install` no longer saves the graph of an automatic rollback from the CLI.

**Migration:** For `nelm release rollback` use `--save-graph-to`. Remove `--save-rollback-graph-to` from `nelm release install` invocations.

**References:** [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### The embedded Helm is upgraded from Helm 3 to Helm 4

<a id="helm-v4-engine"></a>`helm-v4-engine` · change · `charts` `templates` `render` · products: nelm, werf

Before: Nelm embedded a fork of Helm 3 for chart loading, values processing, template rendering, chart repositories and registries.
Now: the embedded fork is based on Helm 4 (v4.2.0): chart loading, values coalescing, `export-values`/`import-values`, the template engine and the chart, repository and registry code follow Helm 4. Root context keys passed with `--set-root-json` still reach templates of the root chart and all subcharts; they can't override the built-in `.Chart`, `.Values`, `.Release`, `.Capabilities`, `.Files` and `.Subcharts`.

**Migration:** Render your charts with the new version and compare the result before deploying: template functions, values coalescing and chart loading follow Helm 4 behavior. See the Helm 4 release notes for changes of the Helm engine.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859), [werf#7793](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7793), [werf#8027](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8027), [werf#8028](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8028), [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a), [nelm@1e1068f13](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/1e1068f13d24), [nelm#627](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/627), [nelm#686](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/686), [nelm#688](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/688), [nelm#743](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/743), [nelm#742](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/742), [nelm@5416f8667](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/5416f866760c)

#### The no-op `--force-adoption` option is removed from render commands

<a id="render-force-adoption-removed"></a>`render-force-adoption-removed` · removal · `render` `cli` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm chart render`, `werf render` and `werf bundle render` accepted `--force-adoption` (`$NELM_FORCE_ADOPTION`, `$NELM_CHART_RENDER_FORCE_ADOPTION`, `$WERF_FORCE_ADOPTION`), which had no effect there.
Now: the option is removed from these commands. Install, plan and rollback commands keep it.

**Migration:** Remove `--force-adoption` from render invocations: an unknown flag fails argument parsing.

**References:** [werf@0b50bd1bb](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/0b50bd1bbf42), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### TypeScript charts are enabled by default and render with Node.js 26+ from the host

<a id="typescript-charts"></a>`typescript-charts` · change · `typescript` `templates` · products: nelm, werf

Before: TypeScript charts (the `ts/` directory of a chart, rendered in addition to or instead of `templates/`) were behind the `NELM_FEAT_TYPESCRIPT=true` feature gate; without it `ts/` was ignored and `chart ts init`/`chart ts build` failed. They were bundled and rendered with Deno 2.7.1, downloaded from GitHub on first use, with `@nelm/chart-ts-sdk` 0.1.x; `--deno-binary-path` (`$NELM_DENO_BINARY_PATH`, `$WERF_DENO_BINARY_PATH`) set an explicit Deno binary.
Now: TypeScript charts are always enabled: a chart with `ts/src` gets its TypeScript manifests rendered, and `chart ts init`, `chart ts build` and `chart pack` (werf: `werf chart ts init`, `werf chart ts build`, `werf bundle publish`) bundle TypeScript without any environment variable. No JavaScript runtime is embedded or downloaded:
- `ts/dist/bundle.js` is built in-process with esbuild (`format: esm`, `platform: node`, `target: node26`); the chart's npm dependencies are installed with the package manager of its lock file (npm, pnpm, yarn or bun) from `PATH`, with package scripts disabled. CommonJS dependencies (kubernetes-models, cdk8s and others) work.
- Rendering, including deploying an already packaged chart, needs Node.js >= 26 from `PATH` or `--node-binary-path` (`$NELM_NODE_BINARY_PATH`, `$WERF_NODE_BINARY_PATH`) on the commands that render: Nelm `chart render`, `chart lint`, `release install`, `release plan install`; werf `converge`, `plan`, `render`, `lint`, `bundle apply`, `bundle plan`, `bundle render`. The bundle runs under `node --permission` with an empty environment, without network, process or out-of-chart file access; this guards against accidental access, not against malicious chart code.
- Charts must use `@nelm/chart-ts-sdk` 0.2.0; `nelm chart ts init` generates a `package.json`-based project.
- `helm package` (Helm's `Package` action, `werf helm package`) packs the chart as it is and no longer builds TypeScript bundles, as in upstream Helm.
Go API: `common.TypeScriptOptions`, `HelmOptions.TypeScriptOpts`, `ts.NewContextWithTSOptions`/`GetTSOptionsFromContext`, `Package.TypeScriptOps`, `ts.RunDenoInstall` and `ts.DownloadDenoForPlatform` are removed; `ts.InstallDependencies` is added; `DenoBinaryPath` is renamed to `NodeBinaryPath` in `ChartRenderOptions`, `ChartLintOptions`, `ReleaseInstallOptions`, `ReleasePlanInstallOptions` and `chart.RenderChartOptions`; `ChartTSInitOptions`, `ChartTSBuildOptions` and `ChartPackOptions` have no runtime path field.

**Migration:** Install Node.js 26 or newer wherever charts with `ts/src` are rendered or deployed (CI runners, deploy images), or pass `--node-binary-path`. A chart with `ts/src` that was deployed without `NELM_FEAT_TYPESCRIPT=true` now renders its TypeScript manifests: remove `ts/` if it was unused. Move TypeScript charts to `@nelm/chart-ts-sdk` 0.2.0 (`chart ts init` shows the new project layout: `package.json` instead of `deno.json`) and rebuild `ts/dist/bundle.js`; bundles built with SDK 0.1.x fail to render. Replace `--deno-binary-path` with `--node-binary-path` on rendering commands and drop it elsewhere; drop `NELM_FEAT_TYPESCRIPT`. Build TypeScript bundles with `nelm chart pack` or `werf bundle publish` instead of `werf helm package`.

**References:** [werf#7725](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7725), [werf#8167](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8167), [werf#8169](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8169), [nelm@cb96a15b9](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/cb96a15b9c26), [nelm@bee47f9cc](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/bee47f9ccbfb), [nelm@615df530c](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/615df530ca9d), [nelm@62d593ff8](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/62d593ff8fb4), [nelm@3abafee78](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/3abafee7837e), [nelm@4c91c3a73](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/4c91c3a739c5), [nelm@bd6de2280](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/bd6de22800ec), [nelm@0b9d576a0](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/0b9d576a0c2e), [nelm#816](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/816), [nelm#826](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/826)

#### Values schema errors are no longer turned into a warning because of service values

<a id="values-schema-validation-service-values"></a>`values-schema-validation-service-values` · change · `values` `validation` · products: nelm, werf

Before: if validating values against `values.schema.json` failed with an error containing `(root): Additional property werf is not allowed` (a schema with `additionalProperties: false` rejecting the injected `werf` service values), the whole validation result was only printed as a warning — including errors about the user's own values — and rendering continued.
Now: on a validation failure caused by service values (`werf`, `global`, ...), validation is repeated without them. If the user's values pass, rendering continues; if they still fail, rendering fails with the error about the user's values. If removing the service values changes which subcharts are enabled, rendering fails and suggests `--no-values-schema-validation`.

**Migration:** Fix values that do not match `values.schema.json`, or fix the schema. To skip the check temporarily, pass `--no-values-schema-validation` (werf: also `WERF_NO_VALUES_SCHEMA_VALIDATION=true`).

**References:** [werf#7756](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7756), [nelm@1c5d25ec2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/1c5d25ec2a27)

#### Whole-chart secret-key rotation commands are removed

<a id="cli-chart-secret-key-rotate-removed"></a>`cli-chart-secret-key-rotate-removed` · removal · `cli` `secrets` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm chart secret key rotate --old-secret-key ... --new-secret-key ... [chart-dir]` re-encrypted `secret-values.yaml` and `secret/*` of a chart with a new key. In werf, `werf helm secret rotate-secret-key [EXTRA_SECRET_VALUES_FILE_PATH...]` re-encrypted `.helm/secret-values.yaml`, the `.helm/secret/` files and the given extra secret values files from the old key (`$WERF_OLD_SECRET_KEY`) to the new one (`$WERF_SECRET_KEY`).
Now: both commands are removed, and werf no longer reads `WERF_OLD_SECRET_KEY`. They missed `.werf-data/secret-values.yaml` of packed charts and subcharts (and, in Nelm, extra secret values files).

**Migration:** Re-encrypt secret files one by one, for the chart, its subcharts and any extra secret values files: decrypt each with the old key and encrypt it with the new one.
- Nelm: `nelm chart secret values-file decrypt` / `nelm chart secret file decrypt` with `--secret-key` set to the old key, then `nelm chart secret values-file encrypt` / `nelm chart secret file encrypt` with the new key.
- werf: `werf helm secret values decrypt` / `werf helm secret file decrypt` with `WERF_SECRET_KEY` set to the old key, then `werf helm secret values encrypt` / `werf helm secret file encrypt` with the new key. The werf documentation on values has a ready-made rotation script.

**References:** [werf#8142](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8142), [nelm#809](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/809)

#### `--fail-on-repo-update-fail` and `--no-update` are removed from the repository commands; `repo update` fails when any repository fails

<a id="cli-repo-update-add-flags-removed"></a>`cli-repo-update-add-flags-removed` · removal · `cli` `charts` · products: nelm, werf

Before: repository update (`nelm repo update`, `werf helm repo update`) only printed a warning when a repository index could not be downloaded and exited successfully unless `--fail-on-repo-update-fail` was passed; repository add (`nelm repo add`, `werf helm repo add`) accepted the deprecated, ignored `--no-update`.
Now: as in Helm 4, repository update always exits with an error `failed to update the following repositories: [...]` when any repository fails, and both `--fail-on-repo-update-fail` and `--no-update` are removed (passing them is an unknown-flag error).

**Migration:** Remove `--fail-on-repo-update-fail` and `--no-update` from scripts. If a failing repository must not fail the command, remove that repository or tolerate the command's exit code.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859), [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a)

#### `--values` and `--set*` override secret values, following the documented precedence

<a id="values-secret-values-precedence"></a>`values-secret-values-precedence` · change · `values` `secrets` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the chart's `secret-values.yaml` and `--secret-values` files overrode `--values` and all `--set*` options, so `--set key=null` could not delete a secret value.
Now: values are layered as documented, from lowest to highest: chart `values.yaml` < chart `secret-values.yaml` < `--values` < `--secret-values` < `--set-json` < `--set` < `--set-string` < `--set-file` < `--set-literal` < werf service values.
- `--set key=null` and `key: null` in `--values` delete keys that come from `secret-values.yaml`; `key: null` in a later `--secret-values` file deletes the key from earlier secret files.
- Subcharts: subchart `values.yaml` < subchart `secret-values.yaml` < parent `values.yaml` (`sub:` section) < parent `secret-values.yaml` (`sub:` section). A null at `sub.key` in the parent's `secret-values.yaml` no longer deletes the subchart's own `sub.key`, as with `values.yaml`.
- `--set a.b=x` fails when `--secret-values` sets `a` to a scalar, as it already did for `--values`.
- The values stored in the release now include the decrypted `--secret-values` (layered between `--values` and `--set*`), so `release get --print-values` (werf: `werf release get --print-values`) shows them, anyone who can read the release storage can read them, and a change in `--secret-values` alone creates a new revision. Releases deployed with `--secret-values` are redeployed once after the upgrade.

**Migration:** If you relied on a secret value overriding the same key from `--values` or `--set*`, remove that key from `--values`/`--set*`. Expect one redeploy of releases that use `--secret-values`, and restrict access to the release storage (Secrets, ConfigMaps or SQL) accordingly, since it now also holds the decrypted `--secret-values`.

**References:** [werf#8117](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8117), [nelm#772](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/772)

#### `.Capabilities.HelmVersion` reports Helm 4

<a id="templates-capabilities-helm-version-v4"></a>`templates-capabilities-helm-version-v4` · change · `templates` `render` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `.Capabilities.HelmVersion.Version` was `v3.14` (the Helm 3 version the embedded fork was based on).
Now: it is the Helm 4 version the embedded fork is based on (`v4.2` at the time of writing). Templates that compare `.Capabilities.HelmVersion` (e.g. `semverCompare "<4.0.0"` or `hasPrefix "v3"`) take a different branch.

**Migration:** Check templates that branch on `.Capabilities.HelmVersion` and make them accept Helm 4 versions.

**References:** [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a)

#### `export-values` and `import-values` apply to `--values`, `--secret-values`, `--set*` and service values

<a id="values-export-import-all-layers"></a>`values-export-import-all-layers` · change · `values` `dependencies` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `export-values` and `import-values` of `Chart.yaml` dependencies were applied to the charts' `values.yaml`/`secret-values.yaml` only (plus maps from user values), so overriding a parent key with `--values`, `--set*` or werf service values (e.g. `global.werf.images.*`) did not reach the subchart, and overriding a child key did not reach the importing parent.
Now: they are applied within each values layer, from lowest to highest: `values.yaml` of all charts with `secret-values.yaml` of subcharts, the root chart's `secret-values.yaml`, `--values`, `--secret-values`, all `--set*` options together, service values. Within a layer an exported value overrides the child key and the parent's own key overrides an imported value; across layers the higher layer wins. Plain values, maps and nulls are exported; nested, multi-level and aliased dependencies are supported, also when the dependency's chart in `charts/` is out of the version range of `Chart.yaml`.
Behavior changes:
- An exported parent value overrides the child key from the same or a lower layer: `--set g.repo=a --set sub.image.repository=b` renders `a`, and service values exported to `sub.image.repository` override `--set sub.image.repository`. A `null` parent value deletes the exported child key.
- A value exported from `secret-values.yaml` overrides the child key set in the same file; a value imported from it overrides the parent key from `values.yaml`.
- Imported values follow user values: `--set sub.out.k=x` changes the parent's imported `k`.
- `--set-json` replacing an export or import source drops the copies exported or imported from lower layers; `--set list[i]=x` over an exported list patches it instead of replacing it.
- Dependency `condition:` values see plain values exported from user values; exported user values no longer appear under subcharts disabled by a condition.
- `--set sub=null` or `sub: null` for a dependency resets the subchart to its defaults instead of failing with `type mismatch on sub`.
- The values stored in the release hold `--values` < `--secret-values` < `--set*` with what `export-values` adds from them, so a release may be redeployed once after the upgrade. For charts with dependencies, the values of the chart stored in the release no longer include `--secret-values` and service values.
- Warnings: an export or import skipped because of its value (a scalar exported to a dependency root, a non-map imported) is reported as a warning, also by `chart pack` (werf: `werf bundle publish`); an `export-values` parent path or `import-values` child path set in no values (e.g. a typo) is reported as `Skipping export-values of "<path>" from chart "<chart>" to dependency "<dep>": the path is not set in any values` or `Skipping import-values of "<path>" from dependency "<dep>" to chart "<chart>": no map is set at the path in any values`. The `ImportValues missing table` warning of the Helm fork is no longer printed.
Go API: `values.Options.MergeSetValues` takes a new last argument `MergeSetValuesOptions`; `ExportUserValues` of the chart v2 util package takes one layer of values and returns the result; `ImportUserValues` is added.

**Migration:** Render your charts with the new version (`nelm chart render` / `werf render`) and compare the output if they use `export-values` or `import-values` together with `--values`, `--set*` or werf service values: a child key you set directly is now overridden by a value exported to it from the same or a higher layer. Set the parent key instead, or remove the export. Expect one redeploy of releases whose stored values change.

**References:** [werf#8117](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8117), [werf#8127](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8127), [werf#8137](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8137), [werf#8135](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8135), [nelm#773](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/773), [nelm#774](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/774), [nelm#775](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/775), [nelm#791](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/791), [nelm#806](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/806)

#### `nelm chart pack` is a native Nelm command that records values, secrets and patches in the chart

<a id="cli-chart-pack-native"></a>`cli-chart-pack-native` · change · `cli` `charts` · products: nelm

Before: `nelm chart pack` wrapped Helm's `package` with its flags (`--version`, `--app-version`, `--sign`, `--key`, `--keyring`, `--passphrase-file`, the kube connection flags, `--registry-config`, `--repository-cache`, `--repository-config`).
Now: `nelm chart pack [chart-dir]` (Go API: `action.ChartPack`) is a native Nelm command with Nelm flag names and `NELM_*` environment variables only: `--chart-version`, `--app-version`, `--chart-name`, `--destination`, `--dependency-update`, `--sign`, `--sign-key`, `--sign-keyring`, `--sign-passphrase-file`, the values flags (`--values`, `--set`, `--set-string`, `--set-json`, `--set-file`, `--set-literal`, `--set-root-json`, `--no-default-values`, `--secret-values`, `--no-default-secret-values`, `--reset-values`), `--patches`, `--no-default-patches`, TypeScript and chart repository flags, among them `--ts-no-rebuild` (`NELM_TS_NO_REBUILD`, `NELM_CHART_PACK_TS_NO_REBUILD`; reuse the existing TypeScript bundle instead of rebuilding it) and `--no-update-chart-repos` (`NELM_NO_UPDATE_CHART_REPOS`, `NELM_CHART_PACK_NO_UPDATE_CHART_REPOS`; don't update the chart repository indexes), both `false` by default. Values, secret values, patches and other inputs are recorded in `.werf-data/` of the packed chart and applied on deploy. Packing an already packed chart adds the new inputs to the recorded ones; `--reset-values` drops them first.
`Chart.yaml` in the packed archive keeps the comments, key order and formatting of the source; only `name`, `version`, `appVersion` and the `helm.sh/images` annotation change. The source `Chart.yaml` is not rewritten. Vendored dependencies are packed as they are; only a missing dependency is downloaded. Charts with `apiVersion: v3` can be packed. `export-values` and `import-values` skipped because of their values are reported as warnings.

**Migration:** Replace the Helm `package` flags in your scripts: `--version` → `--chart-version`, `--key` → `--sign-key`, `--keyring` → `--sign-keyring`, `--passphrase-file` → `--sign-passphrase-file`; drop the kube connection and Helm repository config flags, and use the `--chart-repo-*` flags for chart repositories.

**References:** [nelm#809](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/809), [nelm#821](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/821)

#### `nelm chart upload` is a native Nelm command with `--tag` and an image tag guard

<a id="cli-chart-upload-native"></a>`cli-chart-upload-native` · change · `cli` `charts` `oci` · products: nelm

Before: `nelm chart upload [archive] [remote]` wrapped Helm's `push` with its flags (`--ca-file`, `--cert-file`, `--key-file`, `--insecure-skip-tls-verify`, `--plain-http`, `--registry-config`, `--repository-config`, `--repository-cache`, the kube connection flags).
Now: `nelm chart upload chart-archive remote` (Go API: `action.ChartUpload`) is a native Nelm command with `NELM_*` environment variables only: the chart repository flags (`--chart-repo-ca`, `--chart-repo-cert`, `--chart-repo-key`, `--chart-repo-basic-username`, `--chart-repo-basic-password`, `--insecure-chart-repos`, `--no-verify-chart-repos-tls`, ...) and the repeatable `--tag`. It pushes to `<remote>/<chart name>` under the chart version (`+` as `_`) and the extra tags, with `<archive>.prov` when present, and refuses, before pushing, a tag equal to the tag of an image listed in `helm.sh/images` in the same repository. Loopback registries (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`) are reached over plain HTTP unless TLS options are given.

**Migration:** Replace the Helm `push` flags: `--ca-file` → `--chart-repo-ca`, `--cert-file` → `--chart-repo-cert`, `--key-file` → `--chart-repo-key`, `--insecure-skip-tls-verify` → `--no-verify-chart-repos-tls`, `--plain-http` → `--insecure-chart-repos`; drop the kube connection and Helm registry/repository config flags; registry credentials can be passed with `--oci-chart-repos-creds`.

**References:** [nelm#811](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/811)

#### `nelm release history` is a native command with `-r`/`-n` flags, `--revisions-limit` and structured output

<a id="cli-release-history-native"></a>`cli-release-history-native` · change · `cli` `release-storage` · products: nelm

Before: `nelm release history RELEASE_NAME` was the Helm `history` command: the release was a positional argument, the number of revisions was limited with `--max` (default `256`), output was chosen with `-o table|json|yaml` and had Helm's columns.
Now: `nelm release history -r RELEASE -n NAMESPACE` is a native implementation. The release is passed with `--release`/`-r`, the namespace with `--namespace`/`-n`; `--revisions-limit` (default `0`, no limit) replaces `--max`; `--output-format table|json|yaml` (default `table`) replaces `-o`. The table has `REVISION`, `STATUS`, `DEPLOYED` (RFC 822 date), `CHART`, `CHART VERSION` and `APP VERSION` columns. JSON/YAML output is `{apiVersion: v1, releases: [{name, namespace, revision, status, deployedAt: {human, unix}, annotations, chart: {name, version, appVersion}}]}`. Release storage is chosen with `--release-storage` and `--release-storage-sql-connection`; the usual kube connection flags apply.
The Helm flags and `HELM_*` variables are replaced by the Nelm ones: `--kubeconfig` → `--kube-config` (`$KUBECONFIG` is still read), `--kube-context` (`$HELM_KUBECONTEXT` → `$NELM_KUBE_CONTEXT`), `--kube-apiserver` → `--kube-api-server`, `--kube-as-user` → `--kube-impersonate-user`, `--kube-as-group` → `--kube-impersonate-group`, `--kube-ca-file` → `--kube-ca`, `--kube-tls-server-name` → `--kube-api-server-tls-name`, `--kube-insecure-skip-tls-verify` → `--no-verify-kube-tls`, `--kube-token` (`$HELM_KUBETOKEN` → `$NELM_KUBE_TOKEN`), `--burst-limit` → `--kube-burst-limit`, `--qps` (default `0`) → `--kube-qps-limit` (default `30`), `$HELM_NAMESPACE` → `$NELM_NAMESPACE`, `$HELM_DRIVER` → `--release-storage` (`$NELM_RELEASE_STORAGE`), `$HELM_DRIVER_SQL_CONNECTION_STRING` → `--release-storage-sql-connection` (`$NELM_RELEASE_STORAGE_SQL_CONNECTION`), `--debug`/`$HELM_DEBUG` → `--log-level debug`; `--registry-config`, `--repository-config` and `--repository-cache` are removed.

**Migration:** Replace `nelm release history NAME [-n NS] --max N -o json` with `nelm release history -r NAME -n NS --revisions-limit N --output-format json`, rename the kube connection flags and `HELM_*` environment variables as listed above, and update parsers of the JSON/YAML output to the new structure.

**References:** [nelm@074d35057](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/074d3505764f), [nelm@56c19f14b](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/56c19f14be53), [nelm@2ee2d05ef](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/2ee2d05ef533)

#### `nelm release list` is the native Nelm command, the Helm `list` implementation is removed

<a id="cli-release-list-native"></a>`cli-release-list-native` · change · `cli` `release-storage` · products: nelm

Before: `nelm release list` was the Helm `list` command by default; the native implementation was used only with `NELM_FEAT_NATIVE_RELEASE_LIST=true` or `NELM_FEAT_PREVIEW_V2=true`. Without `-n` it listed releases of the namespace of the current kube context, only `deployed` and `failed` ones by default, and printed a Helm table (`NAME`, `NAMESPACE`, `REVISION`, `UPDATED`, `STATUS`, `CHART`, `APP VERSION`) or, with `-o json|yaml`, a plain array of `{name, namespace, revision, updated, status, chart, app_version}`.
Now: `nelm release list [-n NAMESPACE]` is always the native implementation and the feature gate is removed:
- Without `-n`/`--namespace` releases of all namespaces are listed; the latest revision of every release is shown whatever its status.
- The table has `NAMESPACE` (only when listing all namespaces), `NAME`, `STATUS` and `REVISION` columns. `--output-format json|yaml` (default `table`, `$NELM_OUTPUT_FORMAT`) replaces `-o`/`--output` and prints an object `{apiVersion: v2, releases: [{name, namespace, revision, status, deployedAt: {human, unix}, annotations, chart: {name, version, appVersion}}]}` instead of an array (see `cli-release-list-output-v2`). Releases can be filtered with `--release-label-selector`.
- The Helm `list` flags are removed: `-a`/`--all`, `-A`/`--all-namespaces`, `-d`/`--date`, `--deployed`, `--failed`, `--pending`, `--superseded`, `--uninstalled`, `--uninstalling`, `-f`/`--filter`, `-m`/`--max`, `--offset`, `--no-headers`, `-o`/`--output`, `-r`/`--reverse`, `-l`/`--selector`, `-q`/`--short`, `--time-format`, `--debug`, `--registry-config`, `--repository-config`, `--repository-cache`.
- Kubernetes connection uses the Nelm flags and `NELM_*` variables instead of Helm's flags and `HELM_*` variables: `--kubeconfig` → `--kube-config` (`$KUBECONFIG` is still read), `--kube-context` (`$HELM_KUBECONTEXT` → `$NELM_KUBE_CONTEXT`), `--kube-apiserver` → `--kube-api-server`, `--kube-as-user` → `--kube-impersonate-user`, `--kube-as-group` → `--kube-impersonate-group`, `--kube-ca-file` → `--kube-ca`, `--kube-tls-server-name` → `--kube-api-server-tls-name`, `--kube-insecure-skip-tls-verify` → `--no-verify-kube-tls`, `--kube-token` (`$HELM_KUBETOKEN` → `$NELM_KUBE_TOKEN`), `--burst-limit` → `--kube-burst-limit`, `--qps` (default `0`) → `--kube-qps-limit` (default `30`), `$HELM_NAMESPACE` → `$NELM_NAMESPACE`, `$HELM_DRIVER` → `--release-storage` (`$NELM_RELEASE_STORAGE`), `$HELM_DRIVER_SQL_CONNECTION_STRING` → `--release-storage-sql-connection` (`$NELM_RELEASE_STORAGE_SQL_CONNECTION`), `--debug`/`$HELM_DEBUG` → `--log-level debug`. The other `--kube-*` flags of Nelm (`--kube-config-base64`, `--kube-cert`, `--kube-key`, `--kube-token-path`, ...) are available too.

**Migration:** Remove `NELM_FEAT_NATIVE_RELEASE_LIST`. Pass `-n NAMESPACE` to list one namespace; without it all namespaces are listed. Replace `-o json|yaml` with `--output-format json|yaml` and parse `.releases[]` of the returned object instead of a top-level array (`revision` is a number instead of a string, `chart` is an object `{name, version, appVersion}` instead of `name-version`, `app_version` is `chart.appVersion`, `updated` is `deployedAt.human`). Drop the removed Helm filtering, sorting and paging flags; filter the JSON output instead (e.g. with `jq`) or use `--release-label-selector`. Rename the kube connection flags and `HELM_*` environment variables as listed above.

**References:** [nelm@07f2dfccd](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/07f2dfccdde2)

#### `nelm release uninstall` always uses the native plan-based implementation

<a id="cli-release-uninstall-native"></a>`cli-release-uninstall-native` · change · `uninstall` `cli` · products: nelm

Before: `nelm release uninstall` ran the Helm uninstall action by default; the native implementation was used only with `NELM_FEAT_NATIVE_RELEASE_UNINSTALL=true` or `NELM_FEAT_PREVIEW_V2=true`. In the default mode hook resources of the release were deleted unless `--no-delete-hooks` (`$NELM_RELEASE_UNINSTALL_NO_DELETE_HOOKS`) was set.
Now: the native implementation is always used and the feature gate is removed. Uninstall builds a deletion plan from the last release revision (plus resources present only in the last deployed revision), runs `pre-delete`/`post-delete` hooks, deletes the resources in dependency order and tracks their deletion with the same progress output as `release install`. `--no-delete-hooks` and `$NELM_RELEASE_UNINSTALL_NO_DELETE_HOOKS` are removed. New options: `--delete-propagation` (default `Background`), `--no-remove-manual-changes`, `--save-graph-to` (Graphviz uninstall graph), `--save-report-to` (uninstall report), `--release-storage-sql-connection`, plus `--patches`/`--no-default-patches` and `--log-width`. The kube connection, tracking, `--delete-namespace`, `--release-history-limit`, `--release-storage` and `--timeout` options are unchanged.

**Migration:** Remove `NELM_FEAT_NATIVE_RELEASE_UNINSTALL` and `--no-delete-hooks`/`NELM_RELEASE_UNINSTALL_NO_DELETE_HOOKS` (an unknown flag fails argument parsing). To keep a hook resource on uninstall, annotate it with `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` instead. Check that the uninstall of your releases (hook execution, deletion order and tracking) works as expected; use `--delete-propagation`, `--save-graph-to` and `--save-report-to` to tune and inspect it.

**References:** [nelm@07f2dfccd](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/07f2dfccdde2)

#### `nelm repo` commands move to `nelm chart repo`

<a id="cli-repo-commands-under-chart"></a>`cli-repo-commands-under-chart` · change · `cli` `charts` · products: nelm

Before: chart repository commands were at the top level: `nelm repo add`, `nelm repo remove`, `nelm repo update`, `nelm repo login`, `nelm repo logout`.
Now: they are `nelm chart repo add`, `nelm chart repo remove`, `nelm chart repo update`, `nelm chart repo login`, `nelm chart repo logout`. `nelm repo` no longer exists.

**Migration:** Replace `nelm repo <subcommand>` with `nelm chart repo <subcommand>` in scripts. Some flags of these commands are removed or added with Helm 4: see the separate entries on repository flags (`--no-update` and `--fail-on-repo-update-fail` are removed; `--timeout`, `--plain-http`, `--color`/`--colour` and `--content-cache` are added).

**References:** [nelm#640](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/640)

#### `release get` structured output (`apiVersion: v3`) lists hooks and resources together in `resourceSpecs` and renames `storageLabels` to `labels`

<a id="cli-release-get-resource-specs"></a>`cli-release-get-resource-specs` · change · `cli` `go-api` · products: nelm

Before: the JSON/YAML output of `nelm release get` (`apiVersion: v1`) had separate `hooks` and `resources` lists of raw manifests.
Now: the output has `apiVersion: v3` and a single `resourceSpecs` list with hooks and regular resources together. Each item is `{resourceMeta: {name, namespace, groupVersionKind, filePath, annotations, labels}, unstruct: <manifest>, storeAs}`; hooks are recognized by their `helm.sh/hook` annotation. In the Go API, `action.ReleaseGet` returns a new result type with a `ResourceSpecs []*spec.ResourceSpec` field instead of `ReleaseGetResultV1` with `Hooks` and `Resources`.
