The release labels are reported as `release.labels` instead of `release.storageLabels` (Go API: `ReleaseGetResultV3`, field `Labels` instead of `StorageLabels`).

**Migration:** Update scripts that read `.hooks` or `.resources` to read `.resourceSpecs[].unstruct`, filtering hooks by `.resourceSpecs[].resourceMeta.annotations["helm.sh/hook"]` if needed, to read `.release.labels` instead of `.release.storageLabels`, and to accept `apiVersion: v3`.

**References:** [nelm#612](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/612), [nelm#753](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/753)

#### `release list` structured output has `apiVersion: v2`

<a id="cli-release-list-output-v2"></a>`cli-release-list-output-v2` · change · `cli` `go-api` · products: nelm

Before: the JSON/YAML output of the native `nelm release list` (opt-in in Nelm v1 with `NELM_FEAT_NATIVE_RELEASE_LIST=true` or `NELM_FEAT_PREVIEW_V2=true`; by default `release list` was the Helm `list` command, see `cli-release-list-native`) had `"apiVersion": "v1"`; an empty list could be printed as `null`.
Now: the output has `"apiVersion": "v2"` and an empty list is printed as `"releases": []`; the shape of the release elements is unchanged. A release whose latest revision can't be decoded is listed with `null` details. `--network-parallelism` is accepted but no longer used by `release list`.
Go API: `action.ReleaseList` returns `*ReleaseListResultV2` instead of `*ReleaseListResultV1`. `ReleaseListResultRelease` exposes `Annotations(ctx)`, `Chart(ctx)` and `DeployedAt(ctx)` getters instead of the `Annotations`, `Chart` and `DeployedAt` fields; with `ReleaseListOptions.LegacyMetadataOnly` and `OutputNoPrint`, the release body is read on the first getter call.

**Migration:** Update scripts that check `.apiVersion` of the native `release list` output to accept `v2`. Go API callers: use `*ReleaseListResultV2` and the getters instead of the fields.

**References:** [nelm#745](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/745)

#### `values.schema.json` is validated with JSON Schema draft 2020-12 by default, and schemas themselves are checked

<a id="values-schema-json-schema-2020-12"></a>`values-schema-json-schema-2020-12` · change · `values` `validation` · products: nelm, werf

Before: values were validated against `values.schema.json` with the `gojsonschema` library (JSON Schema drafts 4, 6 and 7); errors looked like `- a: Invalid type. Expected: integer, given: string`.
Now: the Helm 4 validator (`santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6`) is used. A schema without `$schema` is treated as draft 2020-12 (drafts 4, 6, 7 and 2019-09 are used when `$schema` names them), the schema itself must be valid against its metaschema (otherwise rendering fails with `"file:///values.schema.json#" is not valid against metaschema`), `$ref` to `http(s)://` and `file://` URLs are resolved, and unresolved `urn:` references are ignored with a warning. Errors look like `- at '/a': got string, want integer`. A schema valid for the old validator may be rejected, or accept or reject different values, for example when it relies on draft-7-only keywords such as array-form `items`.

**Migration:** Render or lint charts with the new version. Fix schemas reported as invalid against the metaschema, or add `"$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"` to keep draft 7 semantics. Update scripts that parse schema validation error messages.

**References:** [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a)

### Go API

#### Action options take a `DockerConfig` directory, `common.DefaultRegistryCredentialsPath` is removed

<a id="go-api-docker-config-option"></a>`go-api-docker-config-option` · change · `go-api` `registry` · products: nelm

Before: `ChartRenderOptions`, `ChartLintOptions`, `ReleaseInstallOptions` and `ReleasePlanInstallOptions` defaulted `RegistryCredentialsPath` to `common.DefaultRegistryCredentialsPath` (`$DOCKER_CONFIG/config.json` or `~/.docker/config.json`).
Now: these options have a `DockerConfig` field (Docker config directory) and `RegistryCredentialsPath` defaults to `<DockerConfig>/config.json`. `common.DefaultRegistryCredentialsPath` is removed; `common.DefaultDockerConfig` (`~/.docker`, without `$DOCKER_CONFIG`) is added. With both fields empty, `config.json` is looked up relative to the current directory.

**Migration:** Set `DockerConfig` (e.g. to `common.DefaultDockerConfig` or `$DOCKER_CONFIG`) or `RegistryCredentialsPath` explicitly, and replace uses of `common.DefaultRegistryCredentialsPath`.

**References:** [nelm#605](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/605)

#### Actions no longer leave `WERF_SECRET_KEY` set in the process environment

<a id="go-api-secret-key-env-restored"></a>`go-api-secret-key-env-restored` · fix · `go-api` `secrets` · products: nelm

Before: actions given `SecretKey` (`ChartLint`, `ChartRender`, `ReleaseInstall`, `ReleasePlanInstall`, `ReleasePlanShow`, the secret file and values-file actions, etc.) set `WERF_SECRET_KEY` in the process environment and left it there. When Nelm was used as a library, a later action without an explicit key silently used the previous key instead of `.werf_secret_key` / `~/.werf/global_secret_key`, and every child process started later (e.g. kubeconfig exec plugins) inherited it.
Now: after an action returns, `WERF_SECRET_KEY` has its previous value again (or is unset). The unused `GetEncodedSecretValues` method is removed from the legacy `secret.RuntimeData` interface.

**Migration:** If your code relied on an action leaving the key in the environment, pass `SecretKey` to each action or set `WERF_SECRET_KEY` yourself. Remove any implementation or use of `GetEncodedSecretValues` of the legacy secrets runtime data interface.

**References:** [nelm#788](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/788)

#### Logging setup is `action.SetupLogging`, and `action.SetupColorLevel` configures colors alone

<a id="go-api-logging-setup-in-action"></a>`go-api-logging-setup-in-action` · change · `go-api` `logging` · products: nelm

Before: logging was set up with `log.SetupLogging(ctx, logLevel, log.SetupLoggingOptions{ColorMode, LogIsParseable})` from `pkg/log`.
Now: it is `action.SetupLogging(ctx, logLevel log.Level, action.SetupLoggingOptions{...})` in `pkg/action`, with the same `ColorMode` and `LogIsParseable` fields and a new `LogWidth`; `log.SetupLogging` and `log.SetupLoggingOptions` are removed. New `action.SetupColorLevel(opts action.SetupLoggingOptions)` sets only the color level from `ColorMode` and `LogIsParseable`, without resetting the loggers.

**Migration:** Replace `log.SetupLogging` and `log.SetupLoggingOptions` with `action.SetupLogging` and `action.SetupLoggingOptions`.

**References:** [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a), [nelm#620](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/620)

#### Nelm's Go API uses the new kubedog major's packages: `statestore.FailMode` and `statestore.TrackTerminationMode`

<a id="go-api-kubedog-1-types"></a>`go-api-kubedog-1-types` · change · `go-api` `tracking` · products: nelm

Before: Nelm v1 used the kubedog `pkg/trackers/...` layout: the `FailMode` and `TrackTerminationMode` fields of `resource.InstallableResource`, `plan.InstallableResourceInfo` and `plan.OperationConfigTrackReadiness` had the types `multitrack.FailMode` and `multitrack.TrackTerminationMode` from `github.com/werf/kubedog/pkg/trackers/rollout/multitrack`, and `plan.ExecutePlan` and `track.NewProgressTablesPrinter` took stores from `github.com/werf/kubedog/pkg/trackers/dyntracker/{statestore,logstore,util}`.
Now: Nelm depends on the next kubedog major (unreleased; pinned as pseudo-version `v0.13.1-0.20261103160714-1ed920dee18b`, which contains `feat!: new major release 1.0`), where the dynamic tracker moved to `github.com/werf/kubedog/pkg/dyntracker/...` and the legacy `multitrack`, `rollout` and `display` packages are gone. These fields are `statestore.FailMode` and `statestore.TrackTerminationMode` from `github.com/werf/kubedog/pkg/dyntracker/statestore` (same values), and the stores passed to `plan.ExecutePlan` and `track.NewProgressTablesPrinter` come from `github.com/werf/kubedog/pkg/dyntracker/{statestore,logstore,util}`. Kubedog debug output is switched with `github.com/werf/kubedog/pkg/log.SetDebug` instead of `pkg/tracker/debug.SetDebug`.

**Migration:** Upgrade kubedog to the version required by Nelm v2 and replace imports of `github.com/werf/kubedog/pkg/trackers/dyntracker/...` with `github.com/werf/kubedog/pkg/dyntracker/...` and `multitrack.FailMode`/`multitrack.TrackTerminationMode` (and their constants) with the `statestore` ones.

**References:** [nelm@07f2dfccd](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/07f2dfccdde2)

#### Option fields of removed CLI options are removed from the `action` and `common` option structs

<a id="go-api-action-options-removed"></a>`go-api-action-options-removed` · removal · `go-api` `values` `validation` `plan` · products: nelm

Before: the option structs of `pkg/action` and `pkg/common` had fields for options that Nelm v2 removes (see `values-set-runtime-json-removed`, `resource-validation-embedded-schemas`, `plan-show-verbose-diffs-removed`, `render-force-adoption-removed`, `plan-use-plan-release-history-limit`).
Now: these exported identifiers are removed:
- `RuntimeSetJSON` of `common.ValuesOptions`, and therefore of `action.ChartLintOptions`, `ChartRenderOptions`, `ReleaseInstallOptions` and `ReleasePlanInstallOptions`, and `chart.RenderChartOptions.RuntimeSetJSON`: `$.Runtime` is no longer populated.
- `LocalResourceValidation`, `ValidationKubeVersion` and `ValidationSchemas` of `common.ResourceValidationOptions`, and therefore of `common.ReleaseInstallRuntimeOptions` and `action.ChartLintOptions`, `ReleaseInstallOptions`, `ReleasePlanInstallOptions` and `ReleaseRollbackOptions`; the constants `common.DefaultResourceValidationKubeVersion`, `common.DefaultResourceValidationSchema` and `common.APIResourceValidationJSONSchemasCacheDir`; and `resource.ErrResourceValidationSourceSanityCheck`. Validation uses the schemas embedded into the binary; `ValidationExtraSchemas`, `ValidationSkip`, `ValidationSchemaCacheLifetime` and `NoResourceValidation` remain.
- `ShowVerboseDiffs` of `common.ResourceDiffOptions`, and therefore of `action.ReleasePlanInstallOptions` and `ReleasePlanShowOptions`, and the `plan.HiddenVerboseChanges` and `plan.HiddenSensitiveChanges` diff placeholders: diffs of created and deleted resources are always shown, and sensitive values are redacted field by field instead of hiding the whole diff.
- `action.ChartRenderOptions.ForceAdoption`, which had no effect.
- `ReleaseHistoryLimit` of `common.ReleaseInstallRuntimeOptions`, and therefore of `action.ReleasePlanInstallOptions`: it is now a field of `action.ReleaseInstallOptions` only.

**Migration:** Remove these fields from your option literals:
- Pass the data of `RuntimeSetJSON` as values with `ValuesSetJSON` and read it from `.Values` in templates.
- Drop `LocalResourceValidation`, `ValidationKubeVersion` and `ValidationSchemas`; pass your own schema sources with `ValidationExtraSchemas`.
- Drop `ShowVerboseDiffs` and `ForceAdoption`, and stop comparing diffs with `plan.HiddenVerboseChanges`/`plan.HiddenSensitiveChanges`.
- Set `action.ReleaseInstallOptions.ReleaseHistoryLimit` instead of `ReleaseHistoryLimit` in `common.ReleaseInstallRuntimeOptions` or `action.ReleasePlanInstallOptions`.

**References:** [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc), [nelm#673](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/673), [nelm@9d049189c](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/9d049189ce4e), [nelm@65c01393d](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/65c01393de40)

#### Plan artifacts are exposed in the `action` package and returned by `ReleasePlanInstall`

<a id="go-api-plan-artifact-in-action"></a>`go-api-plan-artifact-in-action` · change · `go-api` `plan` · products: nelm

Before: plan artifact types and helpers lived in `pkg/plan` (`plan.PlanArtifact`, `plan.ReadPlanArtifact`, `plan.ValidatePlanArtifact`, `plan.WritePlanArtifact`), and `action.ReleasePlanInstall` returned only `error`; the artifact could be passed between actions only through a file.
Now: they are in `pkg/action` (`action.PlanArtifact`, `action.ReadPlanArtifact`, `action.ValidatePlanArtifact`, `action.WritePlanArtifact`). `action.ReleasePlanInstall` returns `(*action.PlanArtifact, error)`, and `ReleaseInstallOptions.LegacyPlanArtifact` / `ReleasePlanShowOptions.LegacyPlanArtifact` accept an in-memory artifact instead of `PlanArtifactPath`.

**Migration:** Replace `plan.PlanArtifact` and the `plan.*PlanArtifact` functions with their `action.` counterparts, and handle the extra return value of `action.ReleasePlanInstall`.

**References:** [nelm#586](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/586)

#### Release and chart functions work on Helm `Accessor` interfaces, and the release history API is reworked

<a id="go-api-release-chart-accessors"></a>`go-api-release-chart-accessors` · change · `go-api` `release-storage` `charts` · products: nelm

Before: `pkg/release`, `pkg/plan`, `pkg/chart` and `pkg/ts` worked on concrete Helm v3 types (`*release.Release`, `*chart.Chart`, `chartutil.Values`), and `release.History` kept all release bodies in memory.
Now: they work on the version-independent accessors of the Helm fork, `release.Accessor` from `pkg/helm/pkg/release` and `chart.Accessor` from `pkg/helm/pkg/chart`, so v1 and v2 releases and v2 and v3 charts are handled alike (see `chart-api-version-v3`):
- `release.NewRelease(...)` takes a `chart.Accessor` and returns a `release.Accessor`; `release.IsReleaseUpToDate(oldRel, newRel)` takes accessors; `release.ReleaseToResourceSpecs(ctx, rel, releaseNamespace)` takes a context first and an accessor, and no longer has the `noCleanNullFields` argument.
- `plan.BuildReleaseInfos(ctx, deployType, prevReleases []release.Accessor, newRel release.Accessor)` takes accessors; `plan.ReleaseInfo.Release`, `plan.OperationConfigCreateRelease.Release` and `plan.OperationConfigUpdateRelease.Release` are `*release.VersionedRelease` from `pkg/release`, a wrapper with an `Accessor` field.
- `chart.RenderChartResult.Chart` is a `chart.Accessor`; `ts.BundleChartsRecursive` and `ts.RenderChart` take a `chart.Accessor`, and `ts.RenderChart` takes values as `common.Values` from `pkg/helm/pkg/chart/common`.
- The `Status` field of `action.ReleaseGetResultRelease`, `ReleaseInstallResultRelease` and `ReleaseListResultRelease` is `common.Status` from `pkg/helm/pkg/release/common`.
The release history reads revisions as metadata and loads bodies on demand (see `release-storage-metadata-reads`):
- `release.BuildHistory(ctx, releaseName, storage)` takes a context first and no `HistoryOptions`; `release.NewHistory`, `release.BuildHistories` and `release.HistoryOptions` are removed.
- `History.Releases()`, `History.FindAllDeployed()` and `History.FindRevision()` are removed, also from the `Historier` interface; use `History.Revisions()` (revision metadata) and `History.Release(ctx, version)` (loads one body).
- `History.CreateRelease(ctx, rel)` takes an accessor; `History.UpdateRelease(ctx, rel, release.UpdateReleaseOptions)` takes an accessor and options (`KeepDeployedTimestamps`).

**Migration:** Wrap Helm releases and charts with `release.NewAccessor(rel)` / `chart.NewAccessor(chrt)` from `pkg/helm/pkg/release` / `pkg/helm/pkg/chart` and read their data through the accessor methods (`Name()`, `Version()`, `Status()`, `Chart()`, ...). Replace `History.Releases()`/`FindAllDeployed()`/`FindRevision()` with `History.Revisions()` and `History.Release(ctx, version)`, `BuildHistories` with `ReleaseStorager.LatestRevisions` or `ListLatestSummaries`, and pass `release.UpdateReleaseOptions{}` to `UpdateRelease`. Custom `Historier` implementations must follow the new interface (`CreateRelease`, `UpdateRelease`, `DeleteRelease`).

**References:** [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a), [nelm#614](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/614), [nelm@ae98e045c](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/ae98e045c538), [nelm@8f935db93](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8f935db93024), [nelm@e9bbd6e25](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/e9bbd6e25a02), [nelm#723](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/723), [nelm#798](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/798)

#### Release storage is Nelm's own `release` package with a context-aware `ReleaseStorager` and metadata reads

<a id="go-api-release-storage-interface"></a>`go-api-release-storage-interface` · change · `go-api` `release-storage` · products: nelm

Before: release storage was Helm's `storage`/`driver` packages with Nelm extensions; `release.ReleaseStorager` had `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Query` and `GetRelease` working on `*release.Release` without a context, and `NewReleaseStorage` returned `*helmstorage.Storage`.
Now: `pkg/release` implements the Secret, ConfigMap, SQL and memory backends itself, keeping Helm's storage format.
- `ReleaseStorager` methods take `ctx` first and work on release accessors; `Query` and `ListLatestReleases` are removed in favor of `Revisions`, `LatestRevisions`, `LoadRevision`, `LoadRevisionSummary`, `ListRevisionSummaries` and `ListLatestSummaries`, which read metadata only or stream bodies; `UpdateLabels(ctx, name, version, labels)` is added to merge custom labels into a stored revision without creating a new one (existing labels are kept; Helm system labels are not changed).
- Storage errors are `release.ErrReleaseNotFound`, `release.ErrReleaseExists` and `release.ErrReleaseUndecodable`; `driver.ErrReleaseUndecodable` is removed, and `errors.Is(err, driver.ErrReleaseNotFound)` no longer matches errors returned by Nelm.
- `kube.ClientFactorier` gains `Metadata() metadata.Interface`; `kube.ClientFactory` creates the metadata client along with the static and dynamic ones.
- `LatestRevisionsOptions.SkipAnnotations` skips reading release annotations from metadata.

**Migration:** Pass a context to `ReleaseStorager` calls and replace `Query`/`ListLatestReleases` with `Revisions`/`LatestRevisions` (metadata only) or `ListRevisionSummaries`/`ListLatestSummaries` (with bodies). Match storage errors with `errors.Is(err, release.ErrReleaseNotFound)` and its siblings. Custom `kube.ClientFactorier` implementations must add `Metadata() metadata.Interface`.

**References:** [nelm@89f4783bb](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/89f4783bb3dc), [nelm#745](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/745)

#### Resource and plan building functions take a context and no kube client, and use a single `resource.Dependency` type

<a id="go-api-resource-plan-building-changed"></a>`go-api-resource-plan-building-changed` · change · `go-api` `resources` `plan` · products: nelm

Before: `pkg/resource` resolved external dependencies itself, querying the cluster through a `kube.ClientFactorier` when the `Remote` option was set, and kept internal and external dependencies in separate types.
Now: building resources never contacts the cluster, and external dependencies are resolved by the plan (see `dependency-annotations-external-auto`). In `pkg/resource`:
- `BuildResources(ctx, deployType, releaseNamespace, prevRelResSpecs, newRelResSpecs, patchers, opts)` no longer takes a `kube.ClientFactorier`; `BuildResourcesOptions.Remote` and `InstallableResourceOptions.Remote` are removed.
- `NewInstallableResource(ctx, res, otherResSpecs, releaseNamespace, opts)` takes a context first and no `kube.ClientFactorier`.
- `NewDeletableResource(ctx, resourceSpec, otherResourceSpecs, releaseNamespace, opts)` takes a context first and returns `(*DeletableResource, error)`.
- `InternalDependency` and `ExternalDependency` are replaced by `Dependency` (`ResourceMatcher`, `ResourceState`, `External`, `MinMatches`, `MaxMatches`). `InstallableResource.ManualInternalDependencies` and `ExternalDependencies` are replaced by `ManualDependencies`, `DeletableResource.ManualInternalDependencies` by `ManualDependencies`, and `AutoInternalDependencies` of both is `[]*Dependency`.
- `SensitiveInfo.FullySensitive()` is removed (it checked for the whole-resource redaction that no longer exists, see `deploy-sensitive-data-and-stringdata-only`); use the `IsSensitive` and `SensitivePaths` fields.
In `pkg/resource/spec`:
- `NewResourceSpecFromManifest(ctx, manifest, releaseNamespace, opts)` takes a context first.
- `BuildReleasableResourceSpecs` is renamed to `BuildPatchedResourceSpecs`.
- `DropInvalidAnnotationsAndLabelsTransformer`, `NewDropInvalidAnnotationsAndLabelsTransformer` and `TypeDropInvalidAnnotationsAndLabelsTransformer` are removed: invalid annotations and labels fail parsing unless `ResourceSpecOptions.DropInvalidAnnotationsAndLabels` is set (see `render-invalid-annotations-labels-fail`).
- `CleanUnstructOptions.CleanNullFields` and `ResourceSpecOptions.LegacyNoCleanNullFields` are removed: null fields are always cleaned (see `deploy-null-fields-cleaned-by-default`).
In `pkg/plan`, `BuildPlan(ctx, installableInfos, deletableInfos, releaseInfos, releaseNamespace, opts)` takes a context first and the release namespace.

**Migration:** Pass a context to these functions, drop the `kube.ClientFactorier` argument and the `Remote` options, and handle the error of `NewDeletableResource`. Replace `InternalDependency`/`ExternalDependency` with `Dependency` (external ones have `External: true`) and read `ManualDependencies` instead of `ManualInternalDependencies`/`ExternalDependencies`. Call `spec.BuildPatchedResourceSpecs` instead of `BuildReleasableResourceSpecs`, set `ResourceSpecOptions.DropInvalidAnnotationsAndLabels` instead of adding the removed transformer, and pass the release namespace to `plan.BuildPlan`.

**References:** [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc), [nelm#615](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/615), [nelm#614](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/614), [nelm#617](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/617), [nelm#625](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/625), [nelm@e9bbd6e25](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/e9bbd6e25a02), [nelm#755](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/755)

#### The Go module path is `github.com/werf/nelm/v2`

<a id="go-api-module-path-v2"></a>`go-api-module-path-v2` · change · `go-api` · products: nelm

Before: Nelm v1 was imported as `github.com/werf/nelm` (e.g. `github.com/werf/nelm/pkg/action`).
Now: Nelm v2 follows Go semantic import versioning and is imported as `github.com/werf/nelm/v2` (e.g. `github.com/werf/nelm/v2/pkg/action`). The embedded Helm fork moved with it (`github.com/werf/nelm/v2/pkg/helm/...`).

**Migration:** Run `go get github.com/werf/nelm/v2@latest` and replace `github.com/werf/nelm/` with `github.com/werf/nelm/v2/` in your imports.

**References:** [nelm#721](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/721)

#### The `featgate` variables of removed feature gates are removed

<a id="go-api-featgate-removed-gates"></a>`go-api-featgate-removed-gates` · removal · `go-api` · products: nelm

Before: `pkg/featgate` exported `FeatGatePreviewV2`, `FeatGateRemoteCharts`, `FeatGateFieldSensitive`, `FeatGateCleanNullFields`, `FeatGateMoreDetailedExitCodeForPlan`, `FeatGateResourceValidation`, `FeatGateNativeReleaseList`, `FeatGateNativeReleaseUninstall` and `FeatGateCaseInsensitiveConditionTracking`, which library users could enable (e.g. through their `NELM_FEAT_*` environment variables) to opt into the corresponding behavior.
Now: these variables are removed, and their behavior is always on (see `feature-gate-preview-v2-removed` and `tracking-condition-types-case-insensitive`). `FeatGateTypescript` is removed as well (TypeScript charts are always on); only `FeatGatePeriodicStackTraces` and `FeatGateAdoptDeckhouseControllerFields` remain.

**Migration:** Remove references to the removed `featgate.FeatGate*` variables; code paths that checked them should assume they are enabled.

**References:** [nelm@07f2dfccd](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/07f2dfccdde2), [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc), [nelm@0585a1f40](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/0585a1f4041e)

#### The deprecated `ChartDirPath` action option is removed, use `Chart`

<a id="go-api-chart-dir-path-removed"></a>`go-api-chart-dir-path-removed` · removal · `go-api` `charts` · products: nelm

Before: `ChartLintOptions`, `ChartRenderOptions`, `ReleaseInstallOptions` and `ReleasePlanInstallOptions` had a deprecated `ChartDirPath` field, used as the chart when `Chart` was empty.
Now: `ChartDirPath` is removed; only `Chart` is read (a local chart directory, archive, `repo/chart` reference or URL). When `Chart` is empty, the current directory is used.

**Migration:** Set `Chart` instead of `ChartDirPath`.

**References:** [nelm@c0894306f](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/c0894306fd9c)

#### The packages of the embedded Helm fork follow the Helm 4 layout

<a id="go-api-helm-fork-packages-restructured"></a>`go-api-helm-fork-packages-restructured` · change · `go-api` · products: nelm

Before: the Helm fork under `pkg/helm` had the Helm 3 package layout: `pkg/helm/pkg/chart`, `pkg/helm/pkg/chartutil`, `pkg/helm/pkg/release`, `pkg/helm/pkg/releaseutil`, `pkg/helm/pkg/time`, `pkg/helm/pkg/lint`, `pkg/helm/pkg/plugin`, `pkg/helm/pkg/postrender`, `pkg/helm/pkg/phases`, `pkg/helm/pkg/errs`, `pkg/helm/pkg/werf/...` and the Helm CLI in `pkg/helm/cmd/helm`.
Now: it has the Helm 4 layout: v2 charts in `pkg/helm/pkg/chart/v2` (with `.../chart/v2/loader` and `.../chart/v2/util`), version-independent chart code in `pkg/helm/pkg/chart`, `pkg/helm/pkg/chart/loader` and `pkg/helm/pkg/chart/common` (values, capabilities, `chartutil` helpers in `.../chart/common/util`), v3 charts in the internal `pkg/helm/intern/chart/v3`, releases in `pkg/helm/pkg/release/v1` and `pkg/helm/pkg/release/common` (statuses), `releaseutil` in `pkg/helm/pkg/release/v1/util`, post-renderers in `pkg/helm/pkg/postrenderer` and the Helm CLI in `pkg/helm/pkg/cmd`. `pkg/helm/pkg/time`, `pkg/helm/pkg/lint`, `pkg/helm/pkg/plugin`, `pkg/helm/pkg/phases`, `pkg/helm/pkg/errs` and `pkg/helm/pkg/werf/...` are gone. The werf chart options moved from `pkg/helm/pkg/werf/helmopts` to `pkg/common` (`common.HelmOptions`, `common.ContextWithHelmOptions`, `common.LegacyChartType`, `common.TypeScriptOptions`), and the `LegacyChartType` field of `ChartLintOptions`, `ChartRenderOptions`, `ReleaseInstallOptions` and `ReleasePlanInstallOptions` in `pkg/action` is now `common.LegacyChartType`. Many exported functions changed signatures with Helm 4 (e.g. chart loaders take `chart.Charter`, errors are standard `fmt`/`errors` errors instead of `github.com/pkg/errors`).

**Migration:** Update imports to the new package paths (e.g. `pkg/helm/pkg/chart` → `pkg/helm/pkg/chart/v2`, `pkg/helm/pkg/chartutil` → `pkg/helm/pkg/chart/common` or `pkg/helm/pkg/chart/v2/util`, `pkg/helm/pkg/release` → `pkg/helm/pkg/release/v1`, `pkg/helm/cmd/helm` → `pkg/helm/pkg/cmd`, `pkg/helm/pkg/werf/helmopts` → `pkg/common`) and adapt to the Helm 4 signatures; see the Helm 4 SDK changes.

**References:** [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a), [nelm@4c37982b7](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/4c37982b7294)

#### Using Nelm as a Go library requires Go 1.26

<a id="go-api-requires-go-1-26"></a>`go-api-requires-go-1-26` · change · `go-api` · products: nelm

Before: the `go` directive of Nelm v1's `go.mod` was `go 1.23.1`.
Now: Nelm v2 declares `go 1.26.0`, so modules that import it must be built with Go 1.26 or newer.

**Migration:** Build your module with Go 1.26 or newer and raise the `go` directive in your `go.mod` to at least `1.26.0` (`go get` does it when adding `github.com/werf/nelm/v2`).

**References:** [nelm@d08c2937f](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/d08c2937f962)

#### `action.SecretKeyRotate` and `secret.RotateSecretKey` are removed

<a id="go-api-secret-key-rotate-removed"></a>`go-api-secret-key-rotate-removed` · removal · `go-api` `secrets` · products: nelm

Before: `action.SecretKeyRotate(ctx, SecretKeyRotateOptions)` (default log level `action.DefaultSecretKeyRotateLogLevel`) and `pkg/legacy/secret.RotateSecretKey(ctx, helmChartDir, secretWorkingDir, secretValuesPaths...)` re-encrypted the secret values and secret files of a chart with a new key.
Now: `action.SecretKeyRotate`, `action.SecretKeyRotateOptions`, `action.DefaultSecretKeyRotateLogLevel` and `secret.RotateSecretKey` are removed, together with the `nelm chart secret key rotate` command (see `cli-chart-secret-key-rotate-removed`).

**Migration:** Re-encrypt each secret file of the chart, its subcharts and any extra secret values files: decrypt it with `action.SecretValuesFileDecrypt` / `action.SecretFileDecrypt` using the old `SecretKey`, then encrypt it with `action.SecretValuesFileEncrypt` / `action.SecretFileEncrypt` using the new one.

**References:** [nelm#809](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/809)

#### `common` drops the keys of removed dependency annotations and changes `DefaultDeletePropagation` and `DefaultLocalKubeVersion`

<a id="go-api-common-constants-changed"></a>`go-api-common-constants-changed` · change · `go-api` `annotations` · products: nelm

Before: `pkg/common` exported the keys of the legacy dependency annotations, `DefaultDeletePropagation` was `Foreground` and `DefaultLocalKubeVersion` was `"1.20.0"`.
Now:
- `AnnotationKeyHumanDependency`/`AnnotationKeyPatternDependency` (`<name>.dependency.werf.io`), `AnnotationKeyHumanExternalDependency`/`AnnotationKeyPatternExternalDependency` (`<name>.external-dependency.werf.io`), `AnnotationKeyHumanLegacyExternalDependencyResource`/`AnnotationKeyPatternLegacyExternalDependencyResource` (`<name>.external-dependency.werf.io/resource`) and `AnnotationKeyHumanLegacyExternalDependencyNamespace`/`AnnotationKeyPatternLegacyExternalDependencyNamespace` (`<name>.external-dependency.werf.io/namespace`) are removed, as the annotations are no longer supported (see `annotations-legacy-dependency-werf-io-removed` and `annotations-external-dependency-removed`).
- `DefaultDeletePropagation` is `metav1.DeletePropagationBackground` (see `deploy-delete-propagation-background`).
- `DefaultLocalKubeVersion` is `"1.36.0"` (see `render-default-kube-version-1-36`).

**Migration:** Use `AnnotationKeyHumanDeployDependency`/`AnnotationKeyPatternDeployDependency` and `AnnotationKeyHumanDeleteDependency`/`AnnotationKeyPatternDeleteDependency` (`werf.io/deploy-dependency-<name>`, `werf.io/delete-dependency-<name>`) instead of the removed annotation keys. Code that relied on the old defaults through these constants must pass `Foreground` (`ReleaseInstallRuntimeOptions.DefaultDeletePropagation` and the `DefaultDeletePropagation` fields of the action options) or `1.20.0` (`ChartRenderOptions.LocalKubeVersion`, `ChartLintOptions.LocalKubeVersion`) explicitly.

**References:** [nelm@be2f6f8e2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/be2f6f8e20d6), [nelm@2159f9621](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/2159f962147e), [nelm#623](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/623), [nelm#625](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/625)

#### `kube.LegacyClientGetter` and `ClientFactorier.LegacyClientGetter()` are removed

<a id="go-api-kube-legacy-client-getter-removed"></a>`go-api-kube-legacy-client-getter-removed` · removal · `go-api` · products: nelm

Before: `pkg/kube` provided `LegacyClientGetter` (a `genericclioptions.RESTClientGetter` for Helm code, created with `NewLegacyClientGetter`), and the `ClientFactorier` interface and `ClientFactory` had a `LegacyClientGetter()` method.
Now: the type, its constructor and the method are removed.

**Migration:** Use the other `ClientFactorier` methods (`Static()`, `Dynamic()`, `Discovery()`, `Mapper()`, `KubeConfig()`) or build a `RESTClientGetter` from the REST config yourself. Custom `ClientFactorier` implementations no longer need `LegacyClientGetter()`.

**References:** [nelm#663](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/663)

#### `kube.NewKubeConfig` takes the kubeconfig paths from its options

<a id="go-api-kube-new-kube-config-signature"></a>`go-api-kube-new-kube-config-signature` · change · `go-api` · products: nelm

Before: `kube.NewKubeConfig(ctx, kubeConfigPaths []string, opts KubeConfigOptions)` took the kubeconfig paths as a separate argument, and each action split entries of `KubeConnectionOptions.KubeConfigPaths` containing several paths joined with the OS path list separator (`:` on Linux/macOS) itself.
Now: the signature is `kube.NewKubeConfig(ctx, opts KubeConfigOptions)`; the paths are taken from `opts.KubeConnectionOptions.KubeConfigPaths`. Splitting by the path list separator is done by `KubeConnectionOptions.ApplyDefaults`, which still falls back to `~/.kube/config` when neither paths nor `KubeConfigBase64` are set.

**Migration:** Drop the paths argument and set `KubeConfigOptions.KubeConnectionOptions.KubeConfigPaths` instead. Call `KubeConnectionOptions.ApplyDefaults(homeDir)` before `NewKubeConfig` if you pass `KUBECONFIG`-style lists with several paths in one entry.

**References:** [nelm@07f2dfccd](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/07f2dfccdde2)

#### `pkg/export/helm`, `pkg/legacy/deploy`, `action.LegacyReleaseUninstall` and `resource.IsSensitive` are removed

<a id="go-api-legacy-packages-removed"></a>`go-api-legacy-packages-removed` · removal · `go-api` · products: nelm

Before: Nelm v1 had `pkg/export/helm/...`, aliases re-exporting parts of the Helm fork (`action`, `chart`, `chart/loader`, `chartutil`, `cli/values`, `cmd/helm`, `downloader`, `engine`, `getter`, `helmpath`, `kube`, `phases/stages`, `phases/stages/externaldeps`, `postrender`, `registry`, `release`, `releaseutil`, `werf/file`, `werf/helmopts`, `werf/secrets`, `werf/secrets/runtimedata`); `pkg/legacy/deploy` with the Helm-based `ResourcesWaiter` and `StagesSplitter`; `action.LegacyReleaseUninstall` with `LegacyReleaseUninstallOptions` and `DefaultLegacyReleaseUninstallLogLevel`; and `resource.IsSensitive(groupKind, annotations)`.
Now: all of them are removed.

**Migration:** Import the Helm fork packages directly from `pkg/helm/...` (see `go-api-helm-fork-packages-restructured` for the new paths). Use `action.ReleaseUninstall` with `ReleaseUninstallOptions` instead of `action.LegacyReleaseUninstall`. Replace `resource.IsSensitive(gk, annos)` with `resource.GetSensitiveInfo(gk, annos).IsSensitive`. `pkg/legacy/deploy` has no replacement: resource tracking is done by the Nelm plan executor.

**References:** [nelm@07f2dfccd](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/07f2dfccdde2)

#### `resource.ResolveResourcePolicies` is removed

<a id="go-api-resource-policy-resolver-removed"></a>`go-api-resource-policy-resolver-removed` · removal · `go-api` `resources` · products: nelm

Before: `pkg/resource` exported `ResolveResourcePolicies(localRes *InstallableResource, liveMeta *spec.ResourceMeta, releaseNamespace string) []common.ResourcePolicy`, which returned the resource policies of the manifest or, when it had none, the `keep`/`skip-delete` policy of the live object.
Now: the function is removed. Deployments still respect `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` and `werf.io/resource-policy` set on the live object; this is resolved internally by the plan.

**Migration:** Callers of `resource.ResolveResourcePolicies` need their own logic: return `InstallableResource.ResourcePolicies` when it is not empty or when there is no live object (`liveMeta` is nil); otherwise return the `skip-delete` policies from `resource.ResourcePolicies(liveMeta, releaseNamespace)`, which must not be called with a nil `liveMeta`.

**References:** [nelm@79ce86ac0](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/79ce86ac06de)

## Deprecations

### Go API

#### The Helm fork's chart linter and `ProcessDependencies` are deprecated

<a id="go-api-helm-fork-lint-process-dependencies-deprecated"></a>`go-api-helm-fork-lint-process-dependencies-deprecated` · deprecation · `go-api` `values` · products: nelm

Deprecated: `lint.RunAll` and the template lint rules (`rules.Templates`, and `TemplatesWithKubeVersion`/`TemplatesWithSkipSchemaValidation` for v3 charts) of the embedded Helm fork, and `ProcessDependencies` of the chart v2 and v3 util packages. They compute values differently from Nelm's rendering: user values are one layer (`--set*` not separated from `--values`), the root chart's `secret-values.yaml` is coalesced at chart level, and `export-values` run before subcharts are disabled by conditions.

**Migration:** Use `action.ChartLint` instead of the Helm fork's linter, and `chart.RenderChart` instead of `ProcessDependencies`.

**References:** [nelm#800](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/800)

## New features

### General

#### Nelm is published as container images, including `-node` images for TypeScript charts

<a id="distribution-nelm-container-images"></a>`distribution-nelm-container-images` · feature · `distribution` `typescript` · products: nelm

Before: Nelm had no container images; it was installed as a binary.
Now: `ghcr.io/werf/nelm` and `registry.werf.io/werf/nelm` are published for Nelm 2, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, running as the non-root user `nelm` (uid 1000). Variants: `alpine` (default), `ubuntu` and `ubuntu-node`. Tags: `<group>-<channel>-<os>`, `<version>-<os>`, plus `<group>`, `<group>-<channel>`, `<version>`, `latest` for `alpine` and `<group>-node`, `<group>-<channel>-node`, `<version>-node`, `latest-node` for `ubuntu-node`; `latest` and `latest-node` follow group 2, stable.
`ubuntu-node` adds Node.js 26, npm, pnpm, yarn and `git`, so TypeScript charts can be rendered in CI without installing anything; `-node` tags are published only for Nelm 2.4.0 and newer.

**References:** [nelm#825](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/825), <https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/825>

#### `--log-width` sets the width of the log output

<a id="cli-log-width-flag"></a>`cli-log-width-flag` · feature · `cli` `logging` · products: nelm

New: the native `nelm` commands (`release`, `chart` and `version` commands; not the Helm-based `chart download`, `chart dependency download|update` and `chart repo` commands) accept `--log-width <columns>` (`$NELM_LOG_WIDTH`, or the command-specific variable such as `$NELM_RELEASE_INSTALL_LOG_WIDTH`; default `0`, detect automatically). Without a terminal the width falls back to 140 columns; the flag lets CI logs be wider. Go API: `action.SetupLoggingOptions.LogWidth`.

**References:** [nelm@b0b22eb50](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/b0b22eb50bca)

### Deploy

#### A warning is printed when a resource being deployed is already being deleted

<a id="deploy-warn-terminating-resource"></a>`deploy-warn-terminating-resource` · feature · `resources` `logging` · products: nelm, werf

New: install, plan install, rollback and auto-rollback print a warning when the live object of a resource being deployed has `metadata.deletionTimestamp` set (Terminating, e.g. held by a finalizer), saying that it is being deleted and won't be recreated by this deploy; for PersistentVolumeClaims and PersistentVolumes it adds that Pods using it will fail to schedule once recreated and its data may be lost. Before, such an object was silently updated or left as is and could be reported ready. Resources planned for recreation don't get the warning. The plan, tracking and exit code are unchanged.

**References:** [werf#8124](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8124), [nelm#790](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/790)

#### A warning lists secret values in the old format that are read as strings

<a id="secrets-warn-legacy-untyped-values"></a>`secrets-warn-legacy-untyped-values` · feature · `secrets` `values` · products: nelm, werf

Values encrypted in the old format do not store their YAML type and are read as strings, which can make `values.schema.json` checks for `integer`, `boolean` or `number` fail with no hint why.
Now, when a secret values file (including `.werf-data/secret-values.yaml` of a published chart) contains old-format values that would be numbers or booleans as plain YAML, a warning is printed once per file, listing their paths and suggesting to re-enter them with the secret values edit command.

**References:** [werf#8122](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8122), [nelm#796](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/796), [common-go#38](https://github.com/werf/common-go/pull/38)

#### Charts with `apiVersion: v3` are supported

<a id="chart-api-version-v3"></a>`chart-api-version-v3` · feature · `charts` · products: nelm, werf

Before: Nelm v1 did not reject `apiVersion: v3` but treated such charts as `apiVersion: v2`.
Now: charts with `apiVersion: v3` in `Chart.yaml` (the Helm 4 chart format) are handled as such: they can be rendered, linted, packed and deployed, with releases stored in a format Helm reads. For v3 charts:
- subcharts get their own `secret-values.yaml` applied, declared in `dependencies` or not, aliased or not;
- `import-values` apply to every values layer: values.yaml < chart `secret-values.yaml` < `--values` < `--secret-values` < `--set*` < service values;
- `export-values` are not supported: they are ignored with a warning `Ignoring export-values of dependency "<dep>" of chart "<chart>": export-values are not supported in charts with apiVersion v3`.
Release info annotations (`--release-info-annotations`) are stored for v3 charts like for v2 charts.

**References:** [werf#8028](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8028), [werf#8133](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8133), [werf#8129](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8129), [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a), [nelm@ae98e045c](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/ae98e045c538), [nelm@8f935db93](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8f935db93024), [nelm#742](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/742), [nelm#803](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/803), [nelm#795](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/795)

#### Group, version and kind in deploy and delete dependency annotations are matched case-insensitively

<a id="dependency-annotations-gvk-case-insensitive"></a>`dependency-annotations-gvk-case-insensitive` · feature · `annotations` `tracking` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `group`, `version` and `kind` in `werf.io/deploy-dependency-<id>` and `werf.io/delete-dependency-<id>` had to be spelled exactly as in the resource, e.g. `kind=StatefulSet`; `kind=statefulset` did not match the dependency or the cluster resource.
Now: they are compared case-insensitively, both when matching resources of the release and when tracking presence, readiness or absence of external resources, so `kind=statefulset` and `kind=StatefulSet` are equivalent.

**References:** [nelm#626](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/626), [kubedog#394](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/pull/394)

#### Helm-based chart and repository commands get the Helm 4 flags

<a id="cli-chart-commands-helm-4-flags"></a>`cli-chart-commands-helm-4-flags` · feature · `cli` `charts` · products: nelm, werf

The commands built on Helm follow Helm 4 and get new flags.
Nelm (`nelm chart dependency download|update`, `nelm chart download` and the `nelm chart repo` commands):
- all of them: `--color`/`--colour` (`never`, `auto`, `always`) and `--content-cache` (default `~/.cache/helm/content`, a content-addressed cache of downloaded charts);
- `nelm chart dependency download|update`: `--username`, `--password`, `--ca-file`, `--cert-file`, `--key-file`, `--insecure-skip-tls-verify` and `--plain-http` for accessing the chart repository;
- `nelm chart repo login`: `--plain-http`;
- `nelm chart repo add` and `nelm chart repo update`: `--timeout` (default `2m0s`) for downloading the index file.
werf (`werf helm` subcommands; they do not get `--color`/`--colour` or `--content-cache`):
- `werf helm dependency build`, `werf helm dependency update` and `werf helm package`: `--username`, `--password`, `--ca-file`, `--cert-file`, `--key-file`, `--insecure-skip-tls-verify` and `--plain-http` for accessing the chart repository;
- `werf helm registry login`: `--plain-http`;
- `werf helm repo add` and `werf helm repo update`: `--timeout` (default `2m0s`);
- `werf helm repo list`: `--no-headers`.

**References:** [werf@301c8f90d](https://github.com/werf/werf/commit/301c8f90d859), [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a)

#### Nelm commands accept remote charts and `--chart-version` without a feature gate

<a id="charts-remote-charts-enabled"></a>`charts-remote-charts-enabled` · feature · `charts` `cli` · products: nelm

Before: `nelm release install`, `nelm release plan install`, `nelm chart render` and `nelm chart lint` accepted only a local chart directory unless the `remote-charts` or `preview-v2` feature gate was enabled (`NELM_FEAT_REMOTE_CHARTS=true`).
Now: these commands always accept a chart directory, `repo-name/chart-name`, a chart archive or a chart archive URL, and always have `--chart-version`. The feature gate is removed.

**References:** [nelm@8348f9be2](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/8348f9be24bc)

#### Templates can use the Helm 4 functions `fromToml`, `mustToToml`, `mustToYaml` and `toYamlPretty`

<a id="templates-helm-4-functions"></a>`templates-helm-4-functions` · feature · `templates` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `fromToml`, `mustToToml`, `mustToYaml` and `toYamlPretty` were not defined; using them failed rendering with `function "fromToml" not defined`.
Now: chart templates can use them, as in Helm 4: `fromToml` parses a TOML string into a map, `mustToToml` and `mustToYaml` are like `toToml` and `toYaml` but fail rendering on a serialization error instead of returning an empty string or an error message, and `toYamlPretty` renders YAML with 2-space indentation, lists included.

**References:** [nelm@961ca04a4](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/961ca04a485a)

#### `--docker-config` option sets the Docker config directory for OCI chart registry credentials

<a id="charts-docker-config-option"></a>`charts-docker-config-option` · feature · `charts` `registry` `cli` · products: nelm

Before: credentials for OCI chart repositories were read from `$DOCKER_CONFIG/config.json` or `~/.docker/config.json`, overridable only with `--oci-chart-repos-creds` (path to the file).
Now: `nelm chart render`, `nelm chart lint`, `nelm release install` and `nelm release plan install` have `--docker-config` (default `~/.docker`, also read from `$DOCKER_CONFIG` and `$NELM_DOCKER_CONFIG`); credentials are read from `<docker-config>/config.json` unless `--oci-chart-repos-creds` is given.

**References:** [nelm#605](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/605)

#### `--no-values-schema-validation` disables validation of values against `values.schema.json`

<a id="values-schema-validation-disable-option"></a>`values-schema-validation-disable-option` · feature · `values` `validation` `cli` · products: nelm, werf

Before: values were always validated against the chart's `values.schema.json`; there was no way to skip it.
Now: `--no-values-schema-validation` (`$NELM_NO_VALUES_SCHEMA_VALIDATION`; werf: `$WERF_NO_VALUES_SCHEMA_VALIDATION`) skips this validation in `nelm chart render`, `nelm chart lint`, `nelm release install`, `nelm release plan install`, `nelm release rollback` and the corresponding werf deploy, render and lint commands. The Go API has `NoValuesSchemaValidation` in the action options.

**References:** [werf#7756](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7756), [nelm#616](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/616)

#### `chart ts init` creates a runnable TypeScript project with tests

<a id="typescript-chart-scaffold-tests"></a>`typescript-chart-scaffold-tests` · feature · `typescript` `cli` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm chart ts init` and `werf chart ts init` generated `ts/src/index.ts` with the Deployment and Service from Go string templates, without tests.
Now: the scaffold is a runnable Node.js project: `src/index.ts`, `deployment.ts`, `service.ts`, `helpers.ts` and `context.ts`, `src/deployment.test.ts` with `describe`/`it` from `node:test` run by `tsx` on typed render-context fixtures, separate `tsconfig.app.json` and `tsconfig.test.json` projects that editors discover, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run dev:debug` (waits for a debugger with `--inspect-brk`). The rendered Deployment and Service are unchanged; lock files are still created when dependencies are installed.

**References:** [nelm#834](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/834), [nelm#835](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/835), <https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/834>

#### `nelm chart copy` copies a chart with its images between registries and archives

<a id="cli-chart-copy"></a>`cli-chart-copy` · feature · `cli` `charts` `oci` `registry` · products: nelm

New: `nelm chart copy FROM TO` (Go API: `action.ChartCopy`) copies a chart together with every image listed in the `helm.sh/images` annotations of the chart and its dependencies. `FROM` and `TO` are an OCI repository (`oci://REPO[:TAG]`, `docker://REPO[:TAG]` or `REPO[:TAG]`; no tag means `latest`) or an archive (`archive:PATH`, or a path ending in `.tar`, `.tar.gz` or `.tgz`).
- Copied to a repository, the chart is renamed to the repository basename, images are copied by digest into the same repository under their source tags (multi-platform indexes and non-distributable layers included; signatures, SBOMs and other referrers are not), and the image references in `helm.sh/images` are rewritten to `REPO[:TAG]@DIGEST`.
- With `TO` `TAG`, the chart version becomes `TAG` if it is a semver version (without a leading `v`), otherwise `0.0.0-<unix time>-<TAG slug>`; the chart is pushed under the version and `TAG` (`+` pushed as `_`). Without `TAG` it keeps its version.
- Archives are written as an OCI image layout tar; legacy werf bundle archives are also read. `--archive-max-expanded-size` (default `64Gi`) bounds what an archive may expand to.
- An unchanged copy keeps the original chart manifest and provenance; a changed copy is re-signed with `--sign` (`--sign-key`, `--sign-keyring`, `--sign-passphrase-file`), otherwise its provenance is dropped with a warning.
- `--chart-repo-*` credentials and TLS options apply only to the source and destination chart hosts; other image hosts use the Docker credentials store. Loopback registries such as `localhost:5000` are reached over plain HTTP.

**References:** [nelm#810](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/810)

#### `release list --release-label-selector` filters releases by labels of stored revisions

<a id="cli-release-list-label-selector"></a>`cli-release-list-label-selector` · feature · `cli` `release-storage` · products: nelm

New: `release list --release-label-selector <selector>` (default empty; Go API: `ReleaseListOptions.ReleaseLabelSelector`) takes a Kubernetes label selector, applies it to the labels of the stored revisions together with the release namespace, and lists the latest matching revision of each release. Works with Secret, ConfigMap, SQL and memory release storage.

**References:** [nelm#745](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/745)

#### `werf.io/delete-on` controls when resources removed from the chart are deleted

<a id="annotations-delete-on"></a>`annotations-delete-on` · feature · `annotations` `plan` · products: nelm, werf

Before: resources removed from the chart were deleted at a fixed point: before deploying resources on install, upgrade and rollback, and in the main cleanup stage on uninstall.
Now: `werf.io/delete-on` takes comma-separated `install`, `upgrade`, `rollback` and `delete` (uninstall), or their `pre-`/`post-` variants, one per deploy type, and deletes the resource after that stage. The main-stage choice waits for the deployed resources to become ready, so an obsolete resource can stay until its replacement is ready or post hooks have completed. The annotation is read from the previous release, so it must be deployed before the resource is removed from the chart. Omitted deploy types keep the old timing; `werf.io/delete-policy` and `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy` are unchanged. Library consumers get `DeletableResource.DeleteStages`.
Limitations: if a deploy fails before the chosen stage, the resource remains; invalid values stored in the latest release can block upgrade, rollback and uninstall until fixed.

**References:** [nelm#832](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/832), <https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/832>

#### `werf.io/triggers-release: "false"` keeps a resource from causing a new release on its own

<a id="annotations-triggers-release"></a>`annotations-triggers-release` · feature · `annotations` `plan` · products: nelm, werf

New: the `werf.io/triggers-release: "true"|"false"` resource annotation (default `"true"`). With `"false"`, when deciding whether the release is up to date and the deploy can be skipped, Nelm ignores changes in the resource's manifest and all operations on it: creation, update, recreation (e.g. caused by `werf.io/delete-policy: before-creation` or the default delete policy of hooks), deletion and readiness tracking. Useful for Jobs that should run only when something else is deployed (migrations, backups, notifications): without it, a Job with `werf.io/delete-policy: before-creation` is recreated on every deploy, so the release is never skipped.
Adding such a resource to the chart, removing it, or its absence in the cluster (e.g. deleted by `werf.io/delete-policy: succeeded` or `ttlSecondsAfterFinished`) doesn't trigger a release either; it is created or deleted with the next release. Values are always compared as a whole, so changing values used only by such a resource still triggers a release.

**References:** [nelm#779](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/779)

### Go API

#### Progress reports of install and uninstall can include preparation and namespace deletion phases

<a id="go-api-progress-report-phases"></a>`go-api-progress-report-phases` · feature · `go-api` `deploy-report` · products: nelm

New: `LegacyProgressReportPhases: true` in `action.ReleaseInstallOptions` or `action.ReleaseUninstallOptions` makes the snapshots sent to `LegacyProgressReportCh` (`progrep.ProgressReport`) also describe the work outside plan execution: `CurrentPhase` (`Initializing`, `Rendering`, `Analyzing`, `Planning`, `Executing`, `DeletingNamespace`) with `RenderDetails.ResourceCount`, `AnalyzeDetails.Processed`/`Total` and `NamespaceDeleteDetails`. Defaults to `false`: only plan execution is reported, as before, and the phase fields are omitted.
Snapshots at phase boundaries and the final snapshot (sent after the optional release namespace deletion) are sent with a blocking send, so a slow consumer delays the action at these points; intermediate snapshots are still dropped when the channel is full. `BuildResourceInfosOptions.OnResourceAnalyzed` is called for each analyzed resource. See `docs/progress-report.md`.

**References:** [nelm#751](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/751)

#### `ReleaseInstall` can install the result of a previous `ChartRender` without rendering again

<a id="go-api-install-chart-render-result"></a>`go-api-install-chart-render-result` · feature · `go-api` `render` · products: nelm

New: `action.ReleaseInstallOptions.LegacyChartRenderResult` accepts the result of an earlier `action.ChartRender` call. The chart is then not loaded or rendered again and render patches are not reapplied, so exactly the rendered manifests are installed (e.g. after checksumming them to decide whether to install). Render-stage options of `ReleaseInstall` (chart, values, `ExtraAnnotations`/`ExtraLabels`, render patches, etc.) are ignored; install-stage options (diff patches, runtime metadata, release labels, tracking) still apply. `ReleaseInstall` fails with `chart render result release mismatch`, `chart render result release revision mismatch` or `chart render result deploy type mismatch` if the render was made for another release, revision or deploy type. Unset by default.

**References:** [nelm#762](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/762)

## Other changes

### General

#### Published Linux and Windows binaries of Nelm and werf are compressed with upx

<a id="distribution-upx-compressed-binaries"></a>`distribution-upx-compressed-binaries` · change · `distribution` · products: nelm, werf

Before: Nelm and werf release binaries were published uncompressed (Nelm linux/amd64 about 120 MB).
Now: the published Linux and Windows binaries are compressed with upx and unpack themselves in memory on start, so they are much smaller to download: Nelm linux/amd64 is about 70 MB; werf `linux-amd64`, `linux-arm64` and `windows-amd64` binaries distributed via trdl are compressed with `upx --best`. macOS binaries are not compressed.
Some antivirus, EDR or binary-scanning tools flag UPX-packed executables, and tools that inspect the binary (e.g. `go version -m`) cannot read the packed file.

**References:** [werf#7652](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7652), [werf#7744](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7744), [werf#7753](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7753), [nelm#731](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/731)

### Deploy

#### Chart rendering parses each rendered manifest once

<a id="render-performance-single-manifest-parse"></a>`render-performance-single-manifest-parse` · change · `render` `performance` · products: nelm, werf

Before: every rendered manifest was parsed twice, once only to check it.
Now: each manifest is parsed once, which roughly halves the time and allocations of turning rendered templates into resources; the second parse runs only after decoding fails, so error messages for invalid YAML are unchanged. A few YAML inputs that only the discarded check rejected no longer fail rendering: a tab inside a quoted scalar or a plain scalar starting with `@` now render correctly, while for a `...` document-end marker in the middle of a file the rest of the file is dropped, and a YAML-tagged value becomes empty, without an error. Charts that rendered before render the same. Lint (`nelm chart lint`, `werf lint`) still rejects most of these inputs through resource validation; render does not.

**References:** [nelm#730](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/730)

#### Release history is read from storage metadata and release bodies are streamed, cutting memory use

<a id="release-storage-metadata-reads"></a>`release-storage-metadata-reads` · change · `release-storage` `performance` · products: nelm, werf

Before: every action that read release history (`chart render`, `chart lint`, `release plan install`, `release install`, `release rollback`, `release uninstall`, `release list`) fetched and decoded the full body of every stored revision, so time and memory grew with the number and size of revisions; `release list` could run out of memory on clusters with thousands of releases.
Now: revisions are listed from the labels and annotations of the storage objects (Secret, ConfigMap, SQL row) and a revision body is fetched only where the action needs it: `chart render` reads none, `chart lint`, `release plan install`, `release install` and `release uninstall` read the latest one, `release rollback` reads the latest and the target one. `release list` and `release history` stream bodies page by page, keeping only the fields they print; `release list` in table format reads no bodies, and `release history --revisions-limit N` reads only the newest N bodies. The storage format stays Helm-compatible; new revisions additionally carry a `werf.io/release-version: v1` annotation on the storage object, so that release annotations can be read without the body.
Related behavior changes:
- A revision whose body can't be decoded is shown by `release list` and `release history` with its name, namespace, revision and status and `null` details, with an error log, instead of being skipped or replaced by an older revision; history pruning (`--release-history-limit`) now counts and removes such revisions.
- A storage object whose name doesn't match the revision named in its labels, such as a copy of a release Secret, is no longer taken for that revision by listing or pruning.

**References:** [werf#8061](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8061), [werf#8084](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8084), [nelm#723](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/723), [nelm#745](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/745), [nelm#752](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/752)

## Fixes

### General

#### A command-specific environment variable always overrides the global one for the same option

<a id="cli-command-env-var-overrides-global"></a>`cli-command-env-var-overrides-global` · fix · `cli` · products: nelm

Before: when both the global and the command-specific environment variable of a single-value option were set, e.g. `NELM_AUTO_ROLLBACK` and `NELM_RELEASE_INSTALL_AUTO_ROLLBACK`, which of them took effect was random from run to run.
Now: the command-specific variable (`NELM_<COMMAND>_<OPTION>`) always wins over the global one (`NELM_<OPTION>`), as documented. Command-line flags still override both.

**References:** [common-go#32](https://github.com/werf/common-go/pull/32)

### Deploy

#### A release with an internal `state=ready` deploy dependency is skipped when nothing changed

<a id="deploy-skip-unchanged-with-ready-dependency"></a>`deploy-skip-unchanged-with-ready-dependency` · fix · `plan` `tracking` `annotations` · products: nelm, werf

Before: a chart with a resource having an internal `werf.io/deploy-dependency-<id>: state=ready,...` on a resource of the same stage was never considered up to date: every redeploy without changes created a new revision and ran hooks, because the dependency target was always forced into readiness tracking.
Now: readiness tracking of the target is forced only when a resource that depends on it is created, updated, recreated, applied or tracked in the same deploy, so an unchanged release is skipped. A changed target whose dependents are all unchanged is tracked according to its own annotations (`werf.io/fail-mode`, `werf.io/track-termination-mode`) instead of always failing the whole deploy immediately.

**References:** [werf#8123](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8123), [nelm#789](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/789)

#### A release with unchanged numeric `--set` values is skipped as up to date

<a id="deploy-numeric-set-values-up-to-date"></a>`deploy-numeric-set-values-up-to-date` · fix · `values` `plan` · products: nelm, werf

Before: with a number passed by `--set` (e.g. `--set replicas=3`), every `release install` created a new revision and reran hooks, and `release plan install` reported that the release values changed, because the number from `--set` and the same number read back from the stored release were compared as different types.
Now: values are compared by their JSON representation, so an unchanged release is skipped (`Skipped release ...: cluster resources already as desired`) and the plan shows no changes. Real changes, including a number replaced with a string, still create a new revision. Templates still see `--set` numbers as integers.

**References:** [werf#8128](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8128), [nelm#786](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/786)

#### Deploy and delete dependency annotations wait for every matching resource

<a id="dependency-annotations-match-all-resources"></a>`dependency-annotations-match-all-resources` · fix · `annotations` `plan` · products: nelm, werf

Before: when a `werf.io/deploy-dependency-<id>` or `werf.io/delete-dependency-<id>` annotation matched several resources of the release (e.g. no `name` given), the annotated resource waited for only one of them, picked arbitrarily.
Now: it waits for all matching resources to be present, ready or absent, as the annotation requires.

**References:** [nelm@3ef6dc9bd](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/3ef6dc9bdf4b)

#### Deploy doesn't wait for PVCs and PVs removed from the chart to disappear

<a id="deploy-removed-pvc-no-absence-wait"></a>`deploy-removed-pvc-no-absence-wait` · fix · `resources` `tracking` · products: nelm, werf

Before: a PersistentVolumeClaim or PersistentVolume removed from the chart was deleted before the release resources were deployed, and the deploy waited for it to disappear. A PVC stays `Terminating` while old Pods use it (a PV while it is bound), and those Pods are replaced only later in the same deploy, so the deploy hung until the timeout.
Now: on install, upgrade and rollback, removed PVCs and PVs are deleted without waiting for their absence. Explicit dependencies on their absence still wait for them, and `release uninstall` still waits.

**References:** [nelm#777](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/777)

#### Deployment tracking fails fast when the new ReplicaSet cannot create pods

<a id="tracking-deployment-pod-create-failures"></a>`tracking-deployment-pod-create-failures` · fix · `tracking` · products: nelm, werf

Before: when the new ReplicaSet of a Deployment could not create pods (the `ReplicaFailure` condition with reason `FailedCreate`, e.g. `exceeded quota`, an invalid pod spec, or a webhook rejection), tracking only saw transient Warning events, missed failures that happened before tracking started, and usually waited until the tracking timeout.
Now: the `ReplicaFailure` condition of the Deployment's own new ReplicaSet is read directly.
- An invalid pod spec, or a quota shortage that the rollout cannot release by scaling old pods down (confirmed against the pod list and the `ResourceQuota` and held for about 10 seconds), fails the resource immediately, regardless of `werf.io/failures-allowed-per-replica`; with `werf.io/fail-mode: IgnoreAndContinueDeployProcess` the deploy still continues.
- Other pod-create failures, including quota shortages that the rollout can recover from, are counted against `werf.io/failures-allowed-per-replica`, each failure once (previously an event-sourced Deployment failure was counted again on every later status update).
- Confirming a quota deadlock needs `list pods` and `get resourcequotas` in the namespace; without these permissions such failures stay counted.

**References:** [nelm#780](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/780), [kubedog@10db28fc1](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/commit/10db28fc11a0), [kubedog@38643e953](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/commit/38643e953de5), [kubedog@8ceef4c3c](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/commit/8ceef4c3c442), [kubedog@8bcce864f](https://github.com/werf/kubedog/commit/8bcce864f0ad), <https://github.com/werf/kubedog/issues/398>

#### Resources removed from the chart are deleted after a pending or failed revision

<a id="deploy-delete-resources-after-pending-revision"></a>`deploy-delete-resources-after-pending-revision` · fix · `resources` `plan` `uninstall` · products: nelm, werf

Before: deletions were computed only against the last revision. If that revision hung (`pending-upgrade`) or failed before its deletions ran, resources that were in the last deployed revision and were removed from the chart stayed in the cluster forever; `release uninstall` had the same gap and then removed the release history.
Now: `release install`, `release plan install`, `release rollback`, remote `chart lint` and `release uninstall` (werf: `converge`, `plan`, `rollback`, `dismiss`, `bundle apply`, `bundle plan`) also delete the resources that only the last deployed revision has. They are only deleted, never validated or installed, and their hooks don't run. Resources adopted by another release, with `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` or with `werf.io/ownership: anyone` are still not deleted. On the first deploy after such a revision the plan may show extra `delete` operations. Resources left over by earlier deploys whose following revision is already deployed are not cleaned up.

**References:** [werf#8125](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8125), [nelm#792](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/792)

#### Revisions left pending by an interrupted deploy are marked `failed` by the next successful deploy

<a id="release-pending-revisions-marked-failed"></a>`release-pending-revisions-marked-failed` · fix · `release-storage` · products: nelm, werf

Before: if a deploy was interrupted (CI timeout, `kill`) while its revision was `pending-install`, `pending-upgrade` or `pending-rollback`, the revision stayed pending forever, and `release history` (`helm history`) showed an operation in progress that didn't exist.
Now: a successful install, upgrade, rollback or auto-rollback marks every earlier `pending-*` revision `failed` at the end of the deploy, keeping its deployment timestamps. A failed deploy doesn't change them. A pending revision whose body can't be read is skipped with a warning.

**References:** [werf#8131](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8131), [nelm#798](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/798)

#### Rollback expands Lists and converts Secret `stringData` like install

<a id="release-rollback-normalized-stored-manifests"></a>`release-rollback-normalized-stored-manifests` · fix · `rollback` `resources` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `nelm release rollback` and `werf rollback` deployed and stored the manifests of the target revision as they were. For a revision stored without Nelm's normalization (for example by Helm), `kind: List` manifests were not expanded into their items and Secret `stringData` was not converted to `data`, unlike `nelm release install`.
Now: rollback expands Lists and converts Secret `stringData` to base64 `data` before storing the new revision and deploying it, like install. The manifests stored in the rollback revision can therefore differ in form from those of the target revision.

**References:** [nelm#624](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/624)

#### Stopping progress output right after it starts no longer races

<a id="tracking-progress-printer-start-stop-race"></a>`tracking-progress-printer-start-stop-race` · fix · `tracking` `logging` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the periodic progress tables printed during deploy, rollback and uninstall were initialized inside a background goroutine, so stopping or waiting for them immediately after start (e.g. a very short uninstall) could read uninitialized state, which could crash or hang the command.
Now: the printer is fully initialized before its background goroutine starts, so it can be stopped at any time.

**References:** [werf#7805](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/7805), [nelm#690](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/690)

#### Values and dependency messages of the embedded Helm go through the Nelm logger and `--log-level`

<a id="logging-helm-fork-messages-nelm-logger"></a>`logging-helm-fork-messages-nelm-logger` · fix · `logging` `values` · products: nelm, werf

Before: values coalescing warnings (e.g. `cannot overwrite table with non table for ...`) and the `requirements.yaml` deprecation warnings of the embedded Helm were printed only at `--log-level` `debug`/`trace` and to stdout, where they got mixed into `chart render` manifests.
Now: these messages go through the Nelm logger: warnings are shown on stderr at `warning` and `info` levels (hidden at `error`/`silent`, which includes the default level of `chart render`); Helm debug messages are shown at `debug`/`trace`. The values type mismatch error names the full path and types, e.g. `type mismatch on p.mid.leaf: expected a table, got string (some-string)` instead of `type mismatch on leaf: %!t(string=some-string)`, and dependency processing errors name the subchart.

**References:** [werf#8136](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8136), [nelm#805](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/805)

#### `--no-pod-logs` applies when installing from a saved plan and to tracking of dependencies

<a id="plan-use-plan-no-pod-logs"></a>`plan-use-plan-no-pod-logs` · fix · `plan` `tracking` `logging` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `release plan install` didn't apply `--no-pod-logs` to the plan it saved, so `nelm release install --use-plan` (werf: `werf converge --use-plan`) always showed pod logs; readiness tracking for deploy dependencies ignored the flag too.
Now: `--no-pod-logs` is applied whenever a plan is executed, in addition to the `werf.io/skip-logs` annotation.

**References:** [werf#8092](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8092), [nelm@30650512b](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/30650512b08a)

#### `--set`, `--set-file` and `--set-string` values containing commas are parsed as in Helm

<a id="values-set-flags-no-comma-split"></a>`values-set-flags-no-comma-split` · fix · `values` `cli` · products: nelm

Before: the Nelm CLI split the values of `--set`, `--set-file` and `--set-string` (and their `NELM_*` environment variables) on every comma before parsing them, so values with lists or escaped commas, e.g. `--set 'list={a,b}'` or `--set 'key=a\,b'`, were broken into separate invalid assignments.
Now: each flag value is passed as a whole to the Helm parser, which handles `a=1,b=2`, `{a,b}` lists and `\,` escapes the same way as `helm --set`.

**References:** [nelm@64ef06036](https://github.com/werf/nelm/commit/64ef06036d51)

#### `export-values` no longer depend on the order of dependencies in `Chart.yaml`

<a id="values-export-values-dependency-order"></a>`values-export-values-dependency-order` · fix · `values` `dependencies` · products: nelm, werf

Before: `export-values` from the charts' `values.yaml` and `secret-values.yaml` read each dependency's parent values once, in `Chart.yaml` order, so an export whose `parent:` path was written by an export to a sibling dependency listed later got the sibling's default value.
Now: exports are ordered so that an export waits for the exports that write to its `parent:` path, also in nested charts, whichever order the dependencies are listed in. When two exports write the same child path, the one declared later still wins. Ordering many exports is fast (topological sort).

**References:** [werf#8134](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8134), [werf#8138](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8138), [nelm#804](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/804), [nelm#807](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/807)

#### `export-values` of `global.*` declared in a nested chart read the root chart's globals

<a id="values-export-values-nested-global"></a>`values-export-values-nested-global` · fix · `values` `dependencies` · products: nelm, werf

Before: an `export-values` entry with `parent: global.X` declared in an intermediate chart (root → mid → leaf, the export in `mid/Chart.yaml`) read only mid's own `global`, so `--set global.X=...`, `global` in the root `values.yaml` and service values such as `global.werf.images.*` were ignored, and mid's `values.yaml` `global` won over `--set global...`.
Now: such exports read the root chart's `global` merged over the globals of the charts in between, the same way Helm propagates globals to subcharts: the higher chart wins, maps are merged, and between values layers the higher layer still wins.

**References:** [werf#8130](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8130), [nelm#794](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/794)

#### `release get` reports the actual deployment time in `release.deployedAt`

<a id="cli-release-get-deployed-at"></a>`cli-release-get-deployed-at` · fix · `cli` · products: nelm

Before: `nelm release get` always reported the zero time (`0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC`) in `release.deployedAt`.
Now: `release.deployedAt` (`human` and `unix`) is the time the release revision was last deployed.

**References:** [nelm#753](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/753)

#### `secret-values.yaml` of subcharts not listed in `dependencies` is applied

<a id="secrets-subchart-secret-values-undeclared"></a>`secrets-subchart-secret-values-undeclared` · fix · `secrets` `values` `dependencies` · products: nelm, werf

Before: the `secret-values.yaml` of a subchart in `charts/` that the parent doesn't declare in `Chart.yaml` `dependencies` was silently ignored when rendering it as a subchart (it was applied only as a side effect of `export-values` processing of declared dependencies).
Now: every subchart gets its `secret-values.yaml` merged over its `values.yaml`, declared or not, at the same level: subchart `values.yaml` < subchart `secret-values.yaml` < the parent's values for the subchart. `--no-default-secret-values` ignores the `secret-values.yaml` of the subcharts too. Dependency conditions and tags still don't see subchart secret values.

**References:** [werf#8129](https://github.com/werf/werf/pull/8129), [nelm#795](https://github.com/werf/nelm/pull/795)
